headings.title: District creation, noncontiguous territory, and population limit
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes creation of ambulance districts, allows noncontiguous territory within five miles, bars overlapping districts, and excludes counties over 400,000 population except districts operating before August 1, 1998.

headings.title: Corporate status, naming, and general powers
headings.reviewNote: Provides that an organized ambulance district shall be a body corporate and political subdivision known as an ambulance district and may sue and be sued, levy and collect taxes, and issue bonds.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes creation of ambulance districts with noncontiguous territory within five miles, excludes counties over 400,000 population except pre-August 1, 1998 districts, and establishes corporate status and powers.

headings.title: Petition requirements for district formation
headings.reviewNote: Permits voters equal to ten percent of the last gubernatorial vote to file a formation petition with the county clerk and specifies required contents including territory, municipalities, name, minimum population of 2,000, and minimum $10 million assessed valuation.

headings.title: Fire protection district ambulance district formation in charter counties over one million
headings.reviewNote: Permits contiguous chapter 321 fire protection districts in charter counties over one million inhabitants to form a congruent emergency ambulance district if no district exists and the dominant provider as of September 1, 2005 ceases service.

headings.title: Sales tax in lieu of property tax
headings.reviewNote: Permits ambulance districts established on or after August 28, 2011, except in charter counties over one million inhabitants, to levy a sales tax in lieu of a property tax, and requires the formation petition to state the funding tax.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes voter petition requirements for ambulance district formation, St. Louis County fire protection district formation rules, and sales tax in lieu of property tax authorization.

headings.title: Presentation of petition and setting of public hearing
headings.reviewNote: Requires the county clerk to present the formation petition to the county commission, which shall set a hearing within thirty to forty days after filing.

headings.title: Publication or posting of hearing notice
headings.reviewNote: Requires the county commission to give hearing notice by newspaper publication on three separate days or by posting in ten public places at least twenty days before the hearing, specifying required notice contents.

headings.title: Advance payment and reimbursement of notice costs
headings.reviewNote: Requires petitioners to pay printing, publication, or posting costs in advance, to be reimbursed from district funds if the district is organized.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs setting public hearings on ambulance district formation petitions, publication or posting of hearing notice, and advance payment and reimbursement of notice costs.

headings.title: Ballot form for property tax ambulance district
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes the ballot form for organizing an ambulance district authorized to impose a property tax up to thirty cents per one hundred dollars assessed valuation without voter approval.

headings.title: Ballot form for sales tax ambulance district
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes the ballot form for organizing an ambulance district authorized to impose a sales tax up to one-half of one percent without voter approval.

headings.title: Effect of voter approval or rejection of sales tax
headings.reviewNote: Provides that majority voter approval activates the sales tax and requires reducing property tax revenues by fifty percent of prior-year sales tax collections, while rejection bars imposition unless resubmitted and approved.

headings.title: Special trust fund deposit and dedicated use
headings.reviewNote: Requires all revenue received by a district from the authorized tax to be deposited in a special trust fund and used solely for the purposes specified in the ballot proposal.

headings.title: Ambulance District Sales Tax Trust Fund and monthly distribution
headings.reviewNote: Creates the non-state Ambulance District Sales Tax Trust Fund for sales taxes collected by the director of revenue less a one percent collection fee and requires monthly distribution by the tenth day of each month.

headings.title: Refunds, dishonored checks, and tax abolition retention
headings.reviewNote: Permits the director of revenue to make refunds and redeem dishonored checks, requires ninety-day advance notice of tax abolition, and permits one-year retention of two percent of collections before remitting the balance.

headings.title: Applicability of local sales tax administration statutes
headings.reviewNote: Applies sections 32.085 and 32.087 to the sales tax imposed under this section except as modified herein.

entries.reviewSummary: Prescribes ballot forms for property-tax and sales-tax ambulance districts, property tax reduction upon sales tax passage, the Ambulance District Sales Tax Trust Fund, refunds, and chapter 32 applicability.

headings.title: Additional tax levy for central dispatching service
headings.reviewNote: Permits an ambulance district, upon voter approval, to levy an additional tax up to three cents per one hundred dollars assessed valuation solely to provide a central dispatching service.

headings.title: Segregation and disbursement of dispatching tax funds
headings.reviewNote: Requires central dispatching tax funds to be kept separate from all other district funds and paid out only on order of the ambulance district governing body.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes an additional voter-approved ambulance district property tax for central dispatching service and requires separate accounting of the funds.

headings.title: Election subdistricts, at-large directors, terms, and reapportionment
headings.reviewNote: Requires the declaring county commission to divide the district into six numbered subdistricts or provide for six at-large directors, sets staggered one- to three-year initial terms and three-year subsequent terms, requires decennial reapportionment, and continues at-large directors holding office as of August 28, 2026.

headings.title: Candidate qualifications and declaration of candidacy filing
headings.reviewNote: Requires director candidates to be U.S. citizens, district residents for two years, and at least twenty-four years old, and governs filing declarations of candidacy and oaths under section 115.127.

headings.title: Ordinance to abolish election subdistricts
headings.reviewNote: Permits a district board, after a chapter 610 public hearing and two-thirds vote, to adopt an ordinance abolishing election subdistricts if unable to find a qualified candidate for each subdistrict and switching to at-large elections.

headings.title: Ordinance to establish election subdistricts
headings.reviewNote: Permits an ambulance district board, by two-thirds vote, to establish contiguous, compact, equal-population election subdistricts with boundaries set by the county commission and residency required throughout the term.

headings.title: Cancellation of uncontested director elections
headings.reviewNote: Provides that no election shall be held if the number of director candidates does not exceed the number of directors to be elected, and candidates shall assume office as if elected.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs ambulance district election subdistricts and at-large director elections, candidate qualifications and filing, ordinances to abolish or establish subdistricts, and uncontested elections.

headings.title: Board resolution to increase or decrease board membership
headings.reviewNote: Permits six-member boards, by board resolution and voter approval, to increase directors to seven or decrease them to five or three, requiring the resolution to name continuing directors, vacancies, and term end dates.

headings.title: Prescribed ballot form for changing board size
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes the ballot form for voter approval to increase the board to seven members or decrease it to five or three members.

headings.title: Election of additional directors upon increase approval
headings.reviewNote: Requires voters at the next board election after approval of a board increase to select additional persons to fill resulting vacancies.

headings.title: Redrawing of subdistricts and terms upon decrease approval
headings.reviewNote: Requires the county clerk, upon voter approval of a board decrease, to redraw the district into the resulting number of equal-population subdistricts for subdistrict elections under section 190.050 with three-year terms.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes six-member ambulance district boards to submit a voter proposition to increase membership to seven or decrease it to five or three, prescribes ballot language, and governs subsequent elections and subdistrict redrawing.

headings.title: Initial educational training requirement and curriculum
headings.reviewNote: Requires ambulance district board members first elected on or after January 1, 2008 to complete approved educational training covering statutory duties, ethics, sunshine laws, financial responsibility, tax rates, and revenue limits.

headings.title: Continuing education requirement per term
headings.reviewNote: Requires all ambulance district board members to complete three hours of approved continuing education for each term of office.

headings.title: Disqualification and vacancy for failure to complete training
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a board member failing to complete initial and continuing education by the election or appointment anniversary date is immediately disqualified and the office becomes vacant to be filled under section 190.052.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires initial educational training and three hours of continuing education per term for ambulance district board members and provides automatic disqualification and vacancy for failure to complete.

headings.title: Board powers, initial meeting, officers, seal, and bylaws
headings.reviewNote: Vests legislative and executive powers in the board, requires an initial meeting within thirty days to elect a chairman and select officers, and requires defining fiscal years and adopting a corporate seal and bylaws.

headings.title: Duty devotion and reimbursement of actual expenses
headings.reviewNote: Requires board members to devote necessary time to office duties, including state educational programs, and permits reimbursement of actual expenditures incurred on behalf of the district.

headings.title: Additional compensation for board secretary and treasurer
headings.reviewNote: Permits board members serving as secretary or treasurer to receive reasonable additional compensation not exceeding one thousand dollars per year.

headings.title: Board member and chairman meeting attendance fees
headings.reviewNote: Permits attendance fees up to one hundred dollars per meeting (capped at two meetings per month, or four in first-class charter counties) plus fifty dollars per meeting for the chairman up to two meetings per month.

headings.title: Conditions for applicability of board compensation
headings.reviewNote: Restricts compensation under subsections 3 and 4 to districts where the board approves it and to elected terms beginning after August 28, 2000.

headings.title: Twelve-month post-service employment prohibition
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits individual board members from being employed by the board within twelve months after termination of board service unless on a volunteer or uncompensated basis.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes ambulance district board powers, initial organization, expense reimbursement, secretary and treasurer compensation, meeting attendance fees, approval conditions, and a twelve-month post-service employment bar.

headings.title: Subjection to recall and commencement of proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Makes each ambulance district board member subject to recall by registered voters of the election district and permits commencing proceedings by filing a notice of intention.

headings.title: Restrictions on timing and frequency of recall proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Bars commencing recall proceedings if the member has served 180 days or less of the current term, has 180 days or less remaining, or won a recall election during the current term.

headings.title: Service, filing, and contents of notice of intention
headings.reviewNote: Requires serving the notice of intention on the board member, filing it with an affidavit of service with the election authority, and including the member's name, up to 200-word grounds statement, and one to five proponents.

headings.title: Board member written answer to recall statement
headings.reviewNote: Permits the board member within seven days to file and serve a written answer up to 200 words for voter information, providing that statement insufficiencies do not invalidate proceedings.

headings.title: Required contents of recall petition before signing
headings.reviewNote: Requires a recall petition, before any signature is affixed, to include a successor election request, the notice of intention and grounds, the member's answer or a statement of no answer, and signer fields.

headings.title: Affidavit of petition circulator
headings.reviewNote: Requires each submitted petition section to include a signed circulator affidavit stating the circulator's name, address, observation of signatures, belief in genuineness, voter registration in the district, and signature dates.

headings.title: Filing deadline for recall petition
headings.reviewNote: Requires filing the recall petition with the election authority within one hundred eighty days after filing the notice of intention.

headings.title: Required number of qualified signatures
headings.reviewNote: Requires qualified signatures equal to at least twenty-five percent of the votes cast in the most recent gubernatorial election in the election district.

headings.title: Verification and certification by election authority
headings.reviewNote: Requires the election authority within twenty days of filing to determine signature sufficiency, file a certificate of examination results, and provide a copy to proponents upon request.

headings.title: Supplementation of insufficient recall petition
headings.reviewNote: Permits supplementing an insufficient petition within ten days of certification and requires the election authority to certify sufficiency of the supplemented petition within ten days.

headings.title: Effect of insufficient supplemented petition
headings.reviewNote: Provides that no action shall be taken if the supplemented petition remains insufficient, though the petition shall remain on file.

headings.title: Submission and contents of sufficiency certificate to board
headings.reviewNote: Requires the election authority to submit a sufficiency certificate to the board prior to its next meeting stating the member's name and required, total, and valid signature counts.

headings.title: Order of recall election and candidate nominations
headings.reviewNote: Requires the election authority, after board receipt of the certificate, to order a section 115.123 election between 45 and 120 days from receipt and governs nominations by statement of candidacy.

headings.title: Resignation of member prior to recall election
headings.reviewNote: Permits the member to resign at any time prior to forty-two days before the election, removing the recall question from the ballot, declaring the office vacant, and barring the resigning member from filling it.

headings.title: Applicability of chapter 115 and election costs
headings.reviewNote: Applies chapter 115 election conduct and cost payment provisions where appropriate to recall elections under this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes procedures for recalling ambulance district board members, including timing bars, notice of intention, member answer, petition contents, circulator affidavits, signature verification, resignation, and election conduct.

headings.title: Enumerated governmental powers of ambulance district
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates district powers including establishing and operating ambulance services, acquiring property, charging fees, borrowing, contracting, employing staff, providing salaried and volunteer benefits, and purchasing liability insurance without waiving immunity.

headings.title: Reasonable regulation and control of ambulance service
headings.reviewNote: Subjects use of a district's ambulance service to reasonable regulation, control, terms, and conditions established by its board of directors.

headings.title: Suspension or revocation of privileges for ordinance violations
headings.reviewNote: Permits a district regulatory ordinance adopted under this section to provide for suspension or revocation of district-controlled rights or privileges for violations.

headings.title: Supremacy of federal and state laws and regulations
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that nothing in sections 190.001 to 190.245 authorizes a district or board to establish or enforce rules conflicting with applicable federal or state laws or regulations.

headings.title: Public hearing and findings for total management contracts
headings.reviewNote: Requires a board proposing after August 28, 1998 to contract out total management and operation for the first time to hold a public hearing within thirty days and make specified public health and access findings.

headings.title: Waiting period and grandfather exemption for management contracts
headings.reviewNote: Permits entering a management contract sixty days after satisfactory findings with a thirty-day implementation delay, and exempts pre-August 28, 1998 contracts, renewals, modifications, and re-contracting of previously contracted services.

headings.title: Automated external defibrillator requirement for basic life support ambulances
headings.reviewNote: Requires districts authorized to adopt basic life support ambulance rules to require such ambulances to carry an automated external defibrillator and at least one individual trained in its use.

headings.title: Fingerprint criminal background checks for personnel and volunteers
headings.reviewNote: Permits ambulance districts to adopt procedures for state highway patrol and FBI fingerprint criminal history checks on current and prospective employees, contractors, and volunteers with fees under section 43.530.

entries.reviewSummary: Enumerates ambulance district governmental powers, service regulation and ordinance enforcement, federal and state law supremacy, total-management contracting hearings, AED requirements, and fingerprint background checks.

headings.title: Authority to borrow money and issue bonds
headings.reviewNote: Permits the board of directors to borrow money and issue bonds to purchase property or equipment for ambulance service operation, with the loan question submitted to voters by board order.

headings.title: Prescribed ballot form for bond election
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes the substantially required ballot question form for submitting an ambulance district bond borrowing proposition.

headings.title: Board authority upon constitutionally required voter approval
headings.reviewNote: Vests the board, upon approval by the constitutionally required percentage of votes cast and subject to subsection 4, with power to borrow and issue bonds for the ballot-specified amount and purposes.

headings.title: Term, debt limit, interest rate, and sinking fund tax
headings.reviewNote: Limits bond loans to twenty years, caps aggregate district debt at ten percent of taxable tangible property value, caps interest at the highest legal contract rate, and requires an annual tax for interest and a sinking fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes ambulance district boards to borrow money and issue bonds for property or equipment upon voter approval, prescribes the ballot form, and sets maturity, debt, interest, and sinking fund limits.

headings.title: Annexation petition, hearing, and submission order
headings.reviewNote: Requires an annexation petition signed by at least ten percent or fifty voters (whichever is fewer) of the proposed area, a county commission hearing within thirty days, and an election order upon finding compliance.

headings.title: Ballot form for annexation and tax imposition
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes the ballot form submitted to voters in both the existing ambulance district and the proposed annexation area regarding annexation and imposing the existing district tax rate.

headings.title: County commission annexation order upon voter approval
headings.reviewNote: Requires the county commission, within thirty days of certified majority approval, to order the territory annexed, describe the altered boundaries, and file a copy with the county clerk.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes procedures for petitioning to annex land into an ambulance district, county commission hearing, ballot form submitted to voters in both the district and proposed area, and annexation order.

headings.title: Municipal notice of intention of detachment
headings.reviewNote: Permits a qualifying fourth-class city (2,700-3,000 population in a first-class county of 83,000-92,000 population) to file an ordinance-authorized notice of intention of detachment with legal description and map; source notes indicate S.B. 672 (2014) was held unconstitutional in Calzone v. Koster.

headings.title: Public hearing and newspaper notice of detachment
headings.reviewNote: Requires the city after filing notice to publish newspaper notice for three consecutive weeks and hold a public hearing presenting its reasons for detachment and its ambulance service plan.

headings.title: Two-thirds ordinance approval of detachment
headings.reviewNote: Permits the city governing body following the public hearing to approve detachment by an ordinance enacted by two-thirds of all legislative body members.

headings.title: Filing of certified detachment ordinance copies
headings.reviewNote: Requires the city upon enacting the detachment ordinance to file three certified copies with the county assessor and county clerk and one with the election authority if different.

headings.title: Effect of detachment on services, taxes, and existing debt
headings.reviewNote: Ends district service and future taxes upon the ordinance effective date (up to one year after passage) while keeping excluded real property liable for prior outstanding debt and exempting subsequent improvements and personal property.

headings.title: Phased five-year revenue transition fees payable by city
headings.reviewNote: Requires the detaching city to pay the ambulance district declining annual fees from one hundred percent down to one-fifth of prior-year tax revenue over calendar years two through six after detachment.

headings.title: Inapplicability to counties with boundary commissions
headings.reviewNote: Exempts counties in which a boundary commission has been established under sections 72.400 to 72.423 from this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Provides a detachment procedure for a qualifying fourth-class city to exclude territory from an ambulance district with phased five-year fee payments, excludes boundary-commission counties, and carries a source note that S.B. 672 (2014) was held unconstitutional in Calzone v. Koster.

headings.title: Authorization for consolidation of ambulance districts
headings.reviewNote: Permits two or more organized ambulance districts to consolidate into one ambulance district using the procedures in this section.

headings.title: Voter petition for district consolidation
headings.reviewNote: Permits voters equal to ten percent of the last gubernatorial vote in an existing district to file a consolidation petition with the county clerk of the county containing the greater part of the proposed district.

headings.title: Prescribed form of voter consolidation petition
headings.reviewNote: Sets forth the required statutory wording for a voter petition to consolidate existing ambulance districts subject to an attached consolidation plan.

headings.title: Alternative board resolution procedure and form
headings.reviewNote: Permits an alternative consolidation procedure through passage of a prescribed board resolution by the boards of directors of the existing ambulance districts.

headings.title: Required contents of consolidation plan
headings.reviewNote: Requires every petition or resolution to include a consolidation plan detailing the consolidated name, boundaries, proposed tax levy, assets and debts, interim operating district presumption, initial directors, and up to 180-day timeline.

headings.title: Filing, recording, and same-calendar-year deadline
headings.reviewNote: Requires the county clerk to present filed petitions or resolutions and plans to the county commission for recording, and voids proposals not received from all consolidating districts within the same calendar year.

headings.title: Notice of intent, publication, joint hearing, and form
headings.reviewNote: Requires each district to post and publish notice of intent for two consecutive weeks, hold a joint public hearing within thirty days of the second publication, and prescribes the notice form including objection procedures.

headings.title: County commission consolidation order when no objections filed
headings.reviewNote: Requires the county commission, if no objections are filed within thirty days after the public hearing, to order consolidation within forty-five days, appoint plan-named directors, and set the first board meeting.

headings.title: Verification of objections, ballot election, and passage order
headings.reviewNote: Requires county clerk verification of five-percent voter objections, submission of a prescribed consolidation and tax ballot question to voters, and entry of a consolidation and appointment order upon majority approval.

headings.title: Initial tax levy up to highest consolidating rate with voter approval
headings.reviewNote: Permits the consolidated district to impose an initial tax levy up to the highest levy of the consolidating districts if specifically set forth in the voter-approved ballot language.

headings.title: Tax rate cap without resident vote
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits a consolidated district without a resident vote from imposing a property tax or sales tax higher than the lowest existing rate among the consolidating districts.

headings.title: Certification, cessation of prior districts, and transfer of assets
headings.reviewNote: Provides that upon board certification of required licenses, permits, and section 190.053 director training, prior districts cease to exist and the consolidated district assumes all powers, duties, assets, and obligations.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes procedures for consolidating two or more ambulance districts by voter petition or board resolution, required consolidation plans, public hearing and objections, ballot election, tax levy limits, and assumption of powers and obligations.

headings.title: Definitions for first responder vaccination program
headings.reviewNote: Defines bioterrorism, department, director, disaster locations, first responders, and Missouri state highway patrol telecommunicator for this section.

headings.title: Departmental bioterrorism vaccination program
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to offer smallpox, anthrax, and other CDC ACIP-recommended vaccinations to first responders and Highway Patrol telecommunicators exposed at bioterrorism disaster locations.

headings.title: Voluntary participation, safety exception, and medical exemption
headings.reviewNote: Makes vaccination participation voluntary unless the employer determines safe response requires vaccination, requires ACIP contraindication screening, and exempts personnel presenting a licensed physician's written contraindication statement.

headings.title: Vaccination priority during shortages
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director, in consultation with the governor and CDC, to prioritize exposed persons and deployed first responders and Highway Patrol telecommunicators during a vaccine shortage.

headings.title: Notification and education on vaccination program
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to notify first responders and Highway Patrol telecommunicators of program availability and educate them and their employers on offered vaccines and associated diseases.

headings.title: Contracting with health care providers for administration
headings.reviewNote: Permits the department to contract with health care providers, including local public health agencies, hospitals, federally qualified health centers, and physicians, to administer the vaccination program.

headings.title: Contingent effective date upon receipt of federal funding
headings.reviewNote: Makes the section effective only upon receipt of designated federal funding or grants; Revisor's Note states no such federal funding had been received as of the 2016 republication and notes a 2019 St. Louis pilot project.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires the Department of Health and Senior Services to offer a voluntary bioterrorism vaccination program for first responders and Highway Patrol telecommunicators, subject to a contingent federal funding effective date noted by the Revisor as unfulfilled as of 2016.

headings.title: Short title of Public Access to Automated External Defibrillator Act
headings.reviewNote: Provides that this section shall be known and may be cited as the Public Access to Automated External Defibrillator Act.

headings.title: Compliance, maintenance, testing, and inspection duties
headings.reviewNote: Requires a person or entity acquiring an AED to follow placement regulations, maintain and test it per manufacturer guidelines, test at least every two years and after each use, and inspect on-premises devices at least every ninety days.

headings.title: Good-faith civil and criminal immunity for AED use and ownership
headings.reviewNote: Grants civil and criminal immunity to persons gratuitously and in good faith rendering emergency AED care (excluding willful, wanton, or reckless conduct) and extends immunity to AED trainers, site managers, and owners.

headings.title: Mandatory AED equipment on basic life support ambulances and stretcher vans
headings.reviewNote: Requires all basic life support ambulances and stretcher vans operated in Missouri to be equipped with an AED and staffed by at least one individual trained in its use.

headings.title: Statewide applicability across counties and St. Louis City
headings.reviewNote: Provides that this section shall apply in all counties within the state and any city not within a county.

entries.reviewSummary: Enacts the Public Access to Automated External Defibrillator Act, setting maintenance and inspection duties, good-faith civil and criminal immunity, basic life support ambulance and stretcher van equipment mandates, and statewide applicability.

headings.title: Minimum staffing for volunteer-staffed ambulances
headings.reviewNote: Requires a licensed ambulance staffed with volunteer staff to have at least one EMT and one other crew member who may be a licensed EMT, registered nurse, physician, physician assistant, or certified emergency medical responder.

headings.title: Required attendance in patient compartment during transport
headings.reviewNote: Requires at least one licensed EMT, registered nurse, physician assistant, or physician to attend the patient in the patient compartment at all times during transport.

headings.title: Definition of volunteer and nominal stipend allowance
headings.reviewNote: Defines volunteer as an individual serving without promise, expectation, or receipt of compensation, clarifying that nominal per-call stipends for fuel, uniforms, and training do not nullify volunteer status.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes minimum staffing for volunteer-staffed ambulances, requires licensed attendance in the patient compartment during transport, and defines volunteer status including nominal stipends.

headings.title: Definition of community paramedic services
headings.reviewNote: Defines community paramedic services as nonemergent services independent of 911 provided by endorsed entities employing certified community paramedics under medical director supervisory standards and care plans.

headings.title: Eligibility requirements for community paramedic certification
headings.reviewNote: Requires an applicant for community paramedic certification to be a licensed paramedic, complete an approved or accredited certification program, and submit an approved department application.

headings.title: Practice protocols and physician-developed care plans
headings.reviewNote: Requires community paramedics to practice under medical director protocols and supervisory standards and provide care-plan services developed by a physician or collaborative-practice APRN or PA without duplicating other provider services.

headings.title: Inter-service contracts and five-year entity endorsement regulations
headings.reviewNote: Requires written contracts with at least sixty-day cancellation notice to provide community paramedic services in another ambulance service area and directs the department to adopt standards and issue five-year entity endorsements.

headings.title: Applicability of EMS statutes and rules
headings.reviewNote: Subjects community paramedics to sections 190.001 to 190.245 and rules promulgated thereunder.

headings.title: Prohibition on uncertified community paramedic practice
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits any person from holding themselves out as a community paramedic or providing community paramedic services unless certified by the department.

headings.title: Medical director approval of program implementation
headings.reviewNote: Requires the medical director to approve implementation of the community paramedic program.

headings.title: Chapter 536 rulemaking authority and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Subjects rules created under this section to chapter 536 and section 536.028 and declares the section nonseverable from legislative rule-review powers for rules after August 28, 2013.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines community paramedic services, sets certification eligibility and medical director oversight, governs inter-service contracts and five-year entity endorsements, prohibits uncertified practice, and delegates chapter 536 rulemaking authority.

headings.title: Establishment, size, terms, and officers of state EMS advisory council
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the State Advisory Council on Emergency Medical Services of up to twenty-three members serving four-year terms, including the chief paramedic of a city not within a county, with an annually selected chair who may appoint subcommittees.

headings.title: Appointing authorities and association recommendations
headings.reviewNote: Directs the DHSS director to appoint council members from eleven statewide professional association recommendations plus a mobile integrated health care-community paramedicine member, with additional appointments by regional EMS committees and the time-critical diagnosis advisory committee.

headings.title: Recognition of medical director and regional subcommittees
headings.reviewNote: Recognizes the state EMS medical directors advisory committee and regional EMS advisory committees as subcommittees of the council.

headings.title: Geographical and professional representation requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires geographical representation and representation across EMS expertise including volunteers, professional organizations, EMTs, paramedics, nurses, firefighters, physicians, and ambulance and hospital administrators.

headings.title: Ex officio status of state EMS medical director
headings.reviewNote: Designates the state EMS medical director described under section 190.103 as an ex officio member of the council.

headings.title: Uncompensated service and appropriated expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Provides that council and subcommittee members serve without compensation, except that council members shall be reimbursed for reasonable travel and meeting expenses subject to appropriations.

headings.title: Advisory purpose and policy recommendations
headings.reviewNote: Directs the council to advise and make recommendations to the governor, general assembly, and department on policies, plans, procedures, and proposed regulations to improve the statewide EMS system.

headings.title: Standing subcommittee for EMS licensure interstate compact and fee restriction
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a seven-member standing subcommittee to monitor the EMS personnel licensure interstate compact and request live internet public hearings on proposed commission rules, and bars DHSS from raising EMS licensure fees to pay compact assessments.

headings.title: Consultation with time-critical diagnosis advisory committee
headings.reviewNote: Directs the council to consult with the time-critical diagnosis advisory committee described under section 190.257 regarding time-critical diagnosis.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the State Advisory Council on Emergency Medical Services, governing its 23-member composition, appointing authorities, subcommittees, ex officio medical director, expense reimbursement, advisory purpose, interstate compact subcommittee, and time-critical diagnosis consultation.

headings.title: Definitions for peer support counseling program
headings.reviewNote: Defines employee, employer, first responder, peer support advisor, peer support counseling program, peer support counseling session, and record for this section.

headings.title: Confidentiality, subpoena, exceptions, and disciplinary policy
headings.reviewNote: Makes peer support counseling communications confidential and exempt from chapter 610, allows subpoenas for good cause, excludes suicide or homicide threats, mandated reports, criminal admissions, and refusal to perform protective duties, and requires a disciplinary policy for breaches.

headings.title: Employer training, referral authority, and voluntary participation
headings.reviewNote: Subjects employers creating a peer support program to this section, requires advisor counseling training, permits referrals to internal or employer-approved external programs, and prohibits mandating employee participation.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines terms for first responder peer support counseling programs, establishes confidentiality and disclosure exceptions with chapter 610 exemption, and sets employer training, referral, and voluntary participation requirements.

headings.title: Designation and advisory duties of regional EMS committees
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to designate EMS regions and committees by regulation to advise on resource coordination, education, research, protocols, voluntary quality improvement, and time-critical diagnosis plans.

headings.title: Uncompensated service and budgeted expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Provides that committee members serve without compensation, except that the Department of Health and Senior Services shall budget for reasonable travel and meeting expenses.

headings.title: Appointment of members, four-year terms, and medical director
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director to appoint personnel to at least six regional EMS committees for four-year terms from recognized professional organization recommendations and includes the regional EMS medical director as a member.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs designation of regional EMS advisory committees, establishes their advisory duties, provides expense reimbursement without compensation, and governs member appointments and four-year terms.

headings.title: Election and duties of regional and state EMS medical directors
headings.reviewNote: Provides for election of regional EMS medical directors constituting the state EMS medical director's advisory committee, sets initial staggered and subsequent four-year terms, and establishes the state EMS medical director's coordinating role.

headings.title: Services and agencies required to have a medical director
headings.reviewNote: Requires a medical director for all ambulance services and emergency medical response agencies providing advanced life support, medication-assisted basic life support, or invasive basic life support procedures.

headings.title: Standards of care, triage and treatment protocols, and online control
headings.reviewNote: Requires medical directors and agency administrators to ensure care meets standards and establish triage, treatment, and transport protocols, limiting EMTs to approved protocols or direct online medical control.

headings.title: Written agreement and grievance procedures with medical director
headings.reviewNote: Requires ambulance services and emergency medical response agencies needing a medical director to execute a written agreement defining roles, responsibilities, authority, and grievance procedures.

headings.title: Public official status for immunity defenses
headings.reviewNote: Designates elected regional EMS medical directors and the state EMS medical director as public officials for sovereign immunity, official immunity, and Missouri public duty doctrine defenses.

headings.title: Peer review committee status of advisory committee
headings.reviewNote: Designates the state EMS medical director's advisory committee as a peer review committee under section 537.035.

headings.title: Online and offline medical direction for special needs patients
headings.reviewNote: Permits regional EMS medical directors to provide online telecommunication or offline standardized protocol medical direction to AEMTs, EMTs, paramedics, and community paramedics caring for special needs patients or upon local request.

headings.title: Regional treatment protocols for special needs patients
headings.reviewNote: Permits regional EMS medical directors to promulgate multi-jurisdictional treatment protocols for special needs patients requiring advance notice to receiving hospitals of pending arrival, condition, and treatment.

headings.title: Compliance with regional protocols in mass casualty or disaster incidents
headings.reviewNote: Requires multiple EMS agencies, emergency response agencies, and public health departments to take necessary steps to follow subsection 8 regional EMS protocols during mass casualty or state-declared disaster incidents.

headings.title: Non-usurpation of local medical direction authority
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that regional EMS medical directors developing protocols or providing online direction for patients shall not be construed as usurping local medical direction authority.

headings.title: Review of community and regional time-critical diagnosis plans
headings.reviewNote: Requires the state EMS medical directors advisory committee to review and make recommendations on all proposed community and regional time-critical diagnosis plans.

headings.title: Administration of patient's own prescription medications
headings.reviewNote: Permits regional EMS medical directors' online or offline medical directions and treatment protocols to include administration of a patient's own prescription medications.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs election and duties of regional and state EMS medical directors, local medical director requirements and agreements, public official immunity and peer review status, special needs protocols, mass casualty compliance, time-critical diagnosis review, and patient prescription administration.

headings.title: Authorization for pediatric emergency medical services system
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to establish a program to improve pediatric emergency care and implement a comprehensive pediatric EMS system under sections 190.001 to 190.245 and department rules.

headings.title: Acceptance of private contributions, grants, and donations
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to receive contributions, grants, donations, or funds from any private entity to expend for the pediatric EMS program.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes the department to establish a statewide pediatric emergency medical services system and receive private contributions, grants, and donations to fund it.

headings.title: Ambulance service license requirement
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits any person from operating, maintaining, advertising, or engaging in air or ground ambulance patient transportation in Missouri without a currently valid department license.

headings.title: Ground ambulance supervision, staffing, and emergency driving
headings.reviewNote: Requires ground ambulances to be supervised by a licensed EMT (without requiring nurses, physicians, or PAs to hold EMT licenses), staffed by at least two licensed individuals except under section 190.094, and driven by competent operators, with an emergency driving exception.

headings.title: Exemptions for emergency assistance and out-of-state ambulances
headings.reviewNote: Exempts from licensure ambulance services and attendants rendering emergency or catastrophe assistance or operating from outside Missouri to transport patients picked up outside Missouri.

headings.title: Local franchise, contract, or mutual-aid requirements
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that state licensure does not authorize ambulance operation without a franchise in St. Louis City or political subdivisions in counties over 900,000, or without a franchise, contract, or mutual-aid agreement where required by local ordinance.

headings.title: Local ordinances and county-only regulation over 900,000
headings.reviewNote: Allows nonconflicting ordinances by a city not within a county and equally strict or stricter local ordinances elsewhere, except that in counties over 900,000 only the county governing body may adopt such regulations.

headings.title: County ambulance standards in counties over 900,000
headings.reviewNote: Requires the governing body of a county over 900,000 to set standards for all department-licensed ambulance services and prohibits barring any licensed service that meets county standards.

headings.title: Exemption from motor carrier and railroad safety jurisdiction
headings.reviewNote: Provides that ambulance services and vehicles transporting sick, injured, or incapacitated persons shall not be treated as common or contract carriers under the division of motor carrier and railroad safety.

headings.title: Exemption for employer private-property patient transport vehicles
headings.reviewNote: Exempts employer motor vehicles and their operators used to transport employees whose illness or injury occurs on private property rather than public highways or property.

headings.title: Political subdivision authority to operate or contract for service
headings.reviewNote: Permits an authorized political subdivision to operate and manage its own licensed ambulance service and permits any political subdivision to contract with a licensed ambulance service.

headings.title: Limitation on municipal or county regulation inside ambulance or fire districts
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that section 67.300 and section 190.109(2) do not authorize municipalities or counties within an ambulance or ambulance-authorized fire protection district to regulate ambulance services, exempting pre-August 28, 1998 services.

headings.title: Limitation on unfranchised operation inside ambulance or fire districts
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that section 67.300 and section 190.109(2) do not authorize municipalities or counties within an ambulance or ambulance-authorized fire protection district to operate without a franchise where required by ordinance, exempting pre-August 28, 1998 services.

headings.title: Prohibition on discrimination in emergency treatment or transport
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits licensed Missouri ambulance providers from discriminating in emergency patient treatment or transportation based on race, sex, age, color, religion, sexual preference, national origin, ancestry, handicap, medical condition, or ability to pay.

headings.title: Preservation of ambulance district, fire district, and local powers
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that except for subsections 5, 6, 10, and 11, this section does not limit or supersede statutory powers of ambulance districts, chapter 321 fire protection districts, or chapter 67 local governments.

headings.title: Notice and inspection upon sale or transfer of ground ambulance ownership
headings.reviewNote: Requires ground ambulance service owners to notify the department within thirty days of a sale or ownership transfer and directs the department to conduct a licensure compliance inspection.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires state ambulance service licensure, sets ground ambulance staffing and licensing exemptions, defines local franchise and ordinance authority including St. Louis County standards, bars discrimination, preserves district powers, and mandates ownership transfer notice and inspection.

headings.title: Authority to require applicant fingerprint submissions
headings.reviewNote: Permits the Department of Health and Senior Services to require fingerprint submissions as part of applications for EMT, AEMT, or paramedic licensure or EMT-CP certification.

headings.title: Submission of fingerprints to Missouri State Highway Patrol
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department, when requiring fingerprints, to require applicants to submit fingerprints to the Missouri State Highway Patrol for state and federal criminal history background checks.

headings.title: State and FBI records search and department access
headings.reviewNote: Directs fingerprints and fees to the Highway Patrol central repository and FBI under section 43.540, requires notification of results to DHSS, and grants DHSS access to discovered criminal history records notwithstanding section 610.120.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes the Department of Health and Senior Services to require state and federal fingerprint-based criminal history background checks for EMT, AEMT, paramedic, and community paramedic applicants.

headings.title: Authority to enter mutual-aid service contracts
headings.reviewNote: Permits municipal, district, fire protection district, or other ambulance services to enter mutual-aid contracts on agreeable terms, including indefinite terms with at least sixty days' cancellation notice.

headings.title: Emergency assistance upon request of another service
headings.reviewNote: Permits ambulance services to assist any other ambulance service in Missouri upon request during an emergency, major catastrophe, or unforeseen event jeopardizing prompt local response.

headings.title: Applicability of law during mutual-aid or emergency responses
headings.reviewNote: Subjects an ambulance service responding to mutual-aid or emergency aid requests to all provisions of law as if operating within its own jurisdiction.

headings.title: Mutual-aid contracts with neighboring states
headings.reviewNote: Permits mutual-aid contracts between Missouri ambulance services and ambulance services in neighboring states in the same manner as intrastate contracts.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes ambulance services to enter mutual-aid contracts including with neighboring states, render requested emergency assistance, and operate under applicable law during mutual-aid responses.

headings.title: Investigation of air ambulance license applicants
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department, within a reasonable time after receiving an air ambulance license application, to conduct such investigation of the applicant as it deems necessary.

headings.title: Air ambulance licensure authority and rulemaking subjects
headings.reviewNote: Vests the department with authority to license air ambulance services and permits rules covering medical control, staff qualifications, operations, communications, equipment, five-year renewals, quality improvement, and response standards.

headings.title: Prescribed air ambulance license application forms
headings.reviewNote: Requires air ambulance license applications to be made on department-prescribed forms containing information needed to determine compliance with sections 190.001 to 190.245 and rules.

headings.title: Notice and inspection upon sale or transfer of air ambulance ownership
headings.reviewNote: Requires air ambulance service owners to notify the department within thirty days of a sale or ownership transfer and directs the department to conduct a compliance inspection.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs air ambulance service licensing investigations, department rulemaking authority, license application forms, and mandatory notice and inspection upon sale or transfer of ownership.

headings.title: Investigation of ground ambulance license applicants
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department, within a reasonable time after receiving a ground ambulance license application, to conduct such investigation of the applicant as it deems necessary.

headings.title: Grandfathered licensure for December 31, 1997 operators
headings.reviewNote: Directs issuance of a ground ambulance license for the primary service area filed as of December 31, 1997 and August 28, 1998 to persons operating a licensed ambulance on December 31, 1997 who apply and adhere to rules.

headings.title: New or expanded five-year licenses and local endorsement letters
headings.reviewNote: Directs issuance of five-year ground ambulance licenses for new or expanding services upon compliance and requires public-hearing-backed resolution endorsement letters from affected districts, municipalities, or counties stating five public-benefit criteria.

headings.title: Automatic service area expansion and reduction under local contracts
headings.reviewNote: Expands a licensed service's area automatically upon contracting with a political subdivision and reduces it upon contract termination, with an exception for needed services at and around the state fair grounds.

headings.title: Renewal of ground ambulance service licenses
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to renew a ground ambulance service license if the applicant meets statutory and regulatory requirements.

headings.title: Mandatory rulemaking for ground ambulance licensure
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to promulgate rules governing ground ambulance vehicles, equipment, staffing, five-year renewal, records, medical control, communications, MOUs, quality improvement, response standards, regional participation, and administrator qualifications.

headings.title: Prescribed ground ambulance license application forms
headings.reviewNote: Requires ground ambulance license applications to be made on department-prescribed forms containing information needed to determine statutory and regulatory compliance.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs ground ambulance license investigations, 1997 primary service area grandfathering, new or expanded five-year licenses requiring local endorsement letters, contract-based service area changes, renewals, rulemaking, and application forms.

headings.title: Designation and mandatory training of ambulance service administrator
headings.reviewNote: Requires each licensed ambulance service to identify its administrator to the department and requires forty hours of basic operations training and two hours of annual continuing education covering seven specified management and legal topics.

headings.title: Compliance deadline for existing administrators
headings.reviewNote: Gives ambulance service administrators serving as of August 28, 2025 until January 1, 2026 to demonstrate compliance with this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires each licensed ambulance service to designate an ambulance service administrator completing forty hours of basic training and two hours of annual continuing education, with a January 1, 2026 compliance deadline for existing administrators.

headings.title: Mandatory liability insurance or financial responsibility reserves
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits issuing or validating an ambulance license or operating an ambulance without active insurance or adequate financial responsibility reserves for bodily injury, death, and property damage.

headings.title: Submission and director approval prior to licensure
headings.reviewNote: Requires licensees to submit the insurance policy or proof of financial responsibility to the director in specified form for approval prior to issuance of each ambulance service license.

headings.title: Continuing liability, assured insolvency, and permissive operator coverage
headings.reviewNote: Requires policies or self-insurance documents to provide continuing full liability notwithstanding prior recovery, assured insolvency or bankruptcy, nonpayment of premium, or nonrenewal, and to cover judgments against permissive operators.

headings.title: Policy term, thirty-day cancellation notice, and automatic revocation
headings.reviewNote: Requires coverage for the license period, obligates insurers to give at least thirty days' written notice to the director and insured before early cancellation, and automatically revokes licenses upon termination unless replaced.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires continuous liability insurance or financial responsibility reserves for each ambulance, director pre-licensure approval, continuing liability and assured-insolvency provisions, and thirty-day cancellation notice with automatic license revocation.

headings.title: Five-year accreditation or certification of training entities
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to accredit or certify training entities for emergency medical responders, emergency medical dispatchers, and EMTs for five years if statutory requirements are met.

headings.title: Minimum regulatory standards for training programs
headings.reviewNote: Requires department rules to establish minimum standards for entrance criteria, curricula, instructors, facilities, equipment, medical oversight, recordkeeping, and reporting.

headings.title: Prescribed application forms for training entities
headings.reviewNote: Requires training entity applications to be made on department-prescribed forms containing information reasonably necessary to determine compliance.

headings.title: Department review of training entity qualifications
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department upon receiving an application to determine whether the training entity's instructors, facilities, equipment, curricula, and medical oversight meet statutory and regulatory requirements.

headings.title: Issuance of accreditation or certification
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department upon finding requirements satisfied to issue training entity accreditation or certification in accordance with department rules.

headings.title: Periodic compliance review of accredited training entities
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department after issuing accreditation or certification to conduct periodic reviews to assure continued statutory and regulatory compliance.

headings.title: Prohibition on unaccredited or uncertified training
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits any person or entity from holding itself out or providing training required under this section without department accreditation or certification.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs five-year accreditation or certification of EMS training entities, specifies rulemaking subjects, application review, issuance, periodic compliance reviews, and prohibits unaccredited training.

headings.title: Investigation of emergency medical response agency applicants
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department, within a reasonable time after receiving an application, to conduct such investigation as it deems necessary of an emergency medical response agency license applicant.

headings.title: Licensure of advanced life support response agencies and rulemaking
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to license qualifying advanced life support emergency medical response agencies and permits rules covering five-year licensure, medical direction, records and forms, and MOUs with local ambulance services.

headings.title: Prescribed application forms for response agencies
headings.reviewNote: Requires emergency medical response agency license applications to be made on department-prescribed forms containing information needed to determine statutory and regulatory compliance.

headings.title: Prohibition on unlicensed advanced life support response agencies
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits any person or entity from holding itself out as or providing the services of an advanced life support emergency medical response agency without a department license.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs investigation, licensing, rulemaking, application forms, and licensure requirement for emergency medical response agencies providing advanced life support.

headings.title: Applicant investigations and interstate compact criminal background checks
headings.reviewNote: Directs pre-compact applicant investigations, requires post-compact Highway Patrol and FBI background checks at applicant expense with member-state sharing and temporary license allowance, and permits multistate criminal record checks.

headings.title: Five-year EMT licensure, rules, and trafficking training sunset
headings.reviewNote: Directs five-year licensure for all EMT levels and permits rules on age, national education standards, NREMT accreditation and testing, English proficiency, and a one-time four-hour sex and human trafficking relicensure course (effective after March 31, 2027; expires December 31, 2032).

headings.title: Prescribed application forms for EMT licensure
headings.reviewNote: Requires applications for all levels of EMT licenses to be made on department-prescribed forms containing information needed to determine statutory and regulatory compliance.

headings.title: Permitted scope of patient care and protocol additions
headings.reviewNote: Limits EMT patient care to training and experience, the National EMS Scope of Practice Model (with permitted state committee additions for AEMTs and local medical director additions for paramedics), and physician orders or approved protocols.

headings.title: Prohibition on unlicensed EMT practice
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits any person from holding themselves out as an emergency medical technician or providing EMT services without a department license.

headings.title: Chapter 536 rulemaking compliance and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Subjects rules created under this section to chapter 536 and section 536.028 and declares the section nonseverable from legislative rule-review powers for rules after August 28, 2002.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs EMT, AEMT, and paramedic applicant investigations and interstate compact background checks, five-year licensure and rules including a sex and human trafficking training requirement expiring December 31, 2032, application forms, scope of practice, unlicensed practice bar, and chapter 536 rulemaking.

headings.title: Eligibility for ninety-day temporary EMT license
headings.reviewNote: Permits the department to grant a ninety-day temporary EMT license to applicants demonstrating qualifying employment, pending licensure or FBI fingerprint checks, complete application, no prior discipline, and rule compliance.

headings.title: Required immediate supervision during temporary practice
headings.reviewNote: Limits temporary EMT license practice to working under the immediate supervision of an unrestricted Missouri-licensed EMT, registered nurse, physician assistant, or physician.

headings.title: Automatic expiration of temporary EMT license
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a temporary EMT license automatically expires either ninety days from issuance or upon issuance of a five-year EMT license.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes ninety-day temporary EMT licenses for qualifying applicants awaiting licensure or FBI fingerprint verification, requires immediate licensed supervision, and provides automatic expiration.

headings.title: Good-faith immunity for transport, restraint, and personal medication
headings.reviewNote: Shields licensed EMTs acting in good faith without gross negligence from liability for transporting persons under detention applications, restraining at-risk behavioral health patients for safety, or administering necessary personal medications.

headings.title: Preservation of sovereign, official, and public duty immunities
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that nothing in this section creates an exception to sovereign immunity, official immunity, or Missouri public duty doctrine defenses.

entries.reviewSummary: Grants good-faith immunity to licensed EMTs transporting detained behavioral health patients, restraining at-risk behavioral health patients for safety, or administering personal medications, without creating exceptions to governmental immunities.

headings.title: Paramedic authority and prerequisites for behavioral health temporary holds
headings.reviewNote: Permits a crisis-intervention-trained, authorized paramedic acting with another paramedic or health professional under approved protocols to place a patient posing a likelihood of serious harm or significantly incapacitated by alcohol or drugs into a humane temporary hold for transport.

headings.title: Clinical justification and written medical file documentation
headings.reviewNote: Requires every good-faith temporary hold to be clinically appropriate and adequately justified, documented and attested to in writing, and retained in the patient's medical file.

headings.title: Civil immunity and preservation of governmental immunities
headings.reviewNote: Relieves paramedics making good-faith temporary holds from relying on implied consent, grants civil immunity, and preserves sovereign immunity, official immunity, and public duty doctrine defenses for government employees.

headings.title: Required memorandum of understanding with local law enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Requires ambulance services adopting temporary-hold authority to execute an MOU with local law enforcement covering administrative oversight, restraint techniques, field interaction and transport, and quality assurance.

headings.title: Restrictions on physical restraint and medical director review
headings.reviewNote: Permits EMT physical restraint under this section only for imminent danger to bystanders, patient, or personnel, upon direct medical control approval, or with on-scene law enforcement, and requires physician medical director review of all restraint incidents.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes trained paramedics to place qualifying behavioral health or incapacitated patients into temporary holds for transport, requires written justification, provides civil immunity, mandates law enforcement MOUs, and restricts physical restraints.

headings.title: Refusal to issue or renew and right to AHC complaint
headings.reviewNote: Permits the department to refuse issuance or renewal of an endorsement, certificate, permit, or license for noncompliance and requires written notice of reasons and the right to file a chapter 621 AHC complaint.

headings.title: AHC disciplinary complaints and seventeen statutory grounds
headings.reviewNote: Permits the department to file a chapter 621 AHC complaint against current, nonrenewed, or surrendered holders based on seventeen enumerated grounds including impairment, criminal convictions, fraud, incompetence, privacy violations, and dangerous conduct.

headings.title: Licensee rights during department investigation interviews
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department before interviewing an investigated licensee to explain the rights to legal counsel, to have anyone deemed necessary present, and to refuse to answer questions or sign statements without being deemed uncooperative.

headings.title: Chapter 621 proceedings and authorized disciplinary sanctions
headings.reviewNote: Governs AHC proceedings and remediation recommendations and permits the department, only after filing an AHC complaint and finding cause, to censure, impose up to five years' probation, suspend up to three years, or revoke.

headings.title: Relicensure waiting period and permanent bar after two revocations
headings.reviewNote: Requires a one-year wait before applying for discretionary first-time relicensure after revocation and permanently bars relicensure for any individual revoked twice within ten years.

headings.title: Notification to other state licensing authorities
headings.reviewNote: Permits the department to notify proper licensing authorities in other states where a suspended or revoked person was also licensed.

headings.title: Good-faith civil immunity for reporters
headings.reviewNote: Shields any person, organization, association, or corporation reporting or providing information to the department in good faith under sections 190.098 to 190.245 from civil damages.

headings.title: Simultaneous summary suspension for imminent public health threat
headings.reviewNote: Permits simultaneous suspension with an AHC complaint upon finding an imminent public health threat, with notice of basis and a ten-day appeal right requiring a department hearing within ten days.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs refusal, denial, suspension, and revocation of EMS endorsements, certificates, permits, and licenses, enumerates seventeen disciplinary grounds, protects licensee interview rights, sets relicensure bars, shields good-faith reporters, and authorizes imminent-threat summary suspensions.

headings.title: Additional grounds for ground ambulance license sanctions
headings.reviewNote: Permits DHSS to refuse, deny renewal of, or suspend a section 190.109 license or take corrective action based on eight grounds including insolvency, inadequate staffing, over ten percent mutual aid, criminal liability, Medicare or MO HealthNet ineligibility, or administrator or board training failures.

headings.title: Corrective action plan submission and implementation timelines
headings.reviewNote: Permits the department, upon determining insolvency or operational insufficiency under subsection 1, to require submission of a corrective plan within fifteen days and implementation within thirty days.

headings.title: Mandatory notification of insolvency or insufficiency determinations
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to notify neighboring licensees, area legislators, local county and municipal officials, the regional EMS advisory committee, and the state EMS advisory council of insolvency or insufficiency determinations.

headings.title: Engagement with neighboring services for interim and long-term coverage
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to immediately engage neighboring licensees to arrange interim or long-term ground ambulance coverage through service agreements, joint powers agreements, or compensated arrangements.

headings.title: Right of assisting licensees to reasonable compensation and attorney fees
headings.reviewNote: Grants licensees assisting in a suspended licensee's service area the right to seek reasonable compensation covering calls, stand-by time, and daily operating expenses, plus costs and reasonable attorney fees in enforcement actions.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes additional ground ambulance license sanctions for insolvency or operational insufficiency, permits corrective action plans, mandates notifications and neighboring service engagement, and grants assisting services compensation and attorney fees.

headings.title: Confidentiality of complaints and ongoing investigations
headings.reviewNote: Makes complaints, investigatory reports, and applicant or holder information confidential except upon written consent or to authorized agencies, and bars subject access to ongoing investigations until completed under section 190.248(1).

headings.title: Nonconfidentiality of licensee identity, status, and final discipline
headings.reviewNote: Provides that identity, name, address, license, currency, and final disciplinary action for applicants or holders under sections 190.100 to 190.245 shall not be confidential.

headings.title: Nonconfidentiality of ambulance service and training entity contact information
headings.reviewNote: Provides that physical and mailing addresses, phone, fax, email, medical director name, and organizational contact information for licensed ambulance services and certified training entities shall not be confidential.

headings.title: Preservation of other state and federal disclosure laws
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that this section does not authorize releasing department-held records subject to other specific state or federal disclosure laws.

headings.title: Release of aggregate information under section 192.067
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that nothing in this section prohibits the department from releasing aggregate information in accordance with section 192.067.

entries.reviewSummary: Makes EMS complaints and investigatory records confidential until completion while declaring licensee status and organization contact information nonconfidential, preserving other privacy laws, and allowing section 192.067 aggregate data release.

headings.title: Maintenance of accurate patient care records
headings.reviewNote: Requires each ambulance service licensee or emergency medical response agency licensee to maintain accurate records concerning patient care and, if applicable, transportation.

headings.title: Five-year record retention regardless of transfer or closure
headings.reviewNote: Requires licensees to retain records for five years readily available for department inspection, notwithstanding transfer, sale, or discontinuance of the ambulance service or business.

headings.title: Completion of patient care report for each run
headings.reviewNote: Requires completion of a department-approved patient care report for each ambulance run with pertinent remarks by the EMT, registered nurse, or physician and rule-specified items.

headings.title: Interfacility transfer patient care documentation
headings.reviewNote: Requires health care facilities transferring a patient to provide a written or electronic patient care document pertinent to continued care and crew safety, without limiting federal transfer reporting laws.

headings.title: Department inspection during business hours
headings.reviewNote: Requires patient care records to be available for inspection by the department at any reasonable time during business hours.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires ambulance services and emergency medical response agencies to maintain accurate patient care records, retain them for five years despite sale or discontinuance, complete run reports and interfacility transfer documents, and permit business-hours inspection.

headings.title: Uniform ambulance run data collection system and hospital limits
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to administer a uniform data collection system on ambulance runs and injured patients, barring hospital data mandates unless federally required, submitted as of January 1, 1998 under trauma or inpatient rules, or subpoenaed.

headings.title: Civil discovery of otherwise discoverable information
headings.reviewNote: Provides that otherwise discoverable information and documents in any civil action may be obtained from any person or entity providing information under sections 190.001 to 190.245.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs administration of a uniform ambulance run and injured patient data collection system while limiting hospital data disclosure mandates and preserving civil discovery.

headings.title: Class B misdemeanor penalty for violations
headings.reviewNote: Makes any violation of or failure to comply with sections 190.001 to 190.245 a class B misdemeanor.

headings.title: Separate daily offenses and judicial stay of cumulation
headings.reviewNote: Makes each day a violation continues a separate and distinct offense while permitting courts in appropriate cases to stay cumulation of penalties.

headings.title: Concurrent prosecutorial jurisdiction and injunctive proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Grants the attorney general concurrent jurisdiction with prosecuting attorneys to prosecute violations and authorizes either to institute injunctive proceedings.

headings.title: County prosecution of local ambulance ordinance violations
headings.reviewNote: Permits county prosecuting attorneys to prosecute violations of a political subdivision's ambulance laws or ordinances in circuit court and to appoint the subdivision's legal officer as special assistant.

headings.title: Compliance with local franchises and licensure action upon adjudication
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits licensed ambulance services from operating without or violating required local franchises, contracts, or mutual-aid agreements and subjects adjudicated violators to department licensure action upon official notice.

headings.title: Preservation of political subdivision enforcement authority
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that this section does not limit or supersede a political subdivision's right to enforce any law, ordinance, regulation, franchise, contract, or mutual-aid agreement.

headings.title: Exemption for St. Louis City and counties over 900,000
headings.reviewNote: Exempts a city not within a county, counties over 900,000 inhabitants, and licensed ambulance services operating in a city not within a county from subsections 4, 5, and 6.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes class B misdemeanor penalties and separate daily offenses for EMS statutory violations, grants concurrent prosecutorial and injunctive authority, addresses local ambulance ordinance prosecutions and licensure actions, and exempts St. Louis City and counties over 900,000 from subsections 4 to 6.

headings.title: One-year extension for existing ambulance vehicle and aircraft licenses
headings.reviewNote: Extends the expiration date of valid or qualified ambulance vehicle or aircraft licenses on the effective date of sections 190.001 to 190.245 to one year after that effective date.

headings.title: August 28, 1999 compliance deadline and staggered initial licensing
headings.reviewNote: Grants ambulance services until August 28, 1999 to comply with sections 190.001 to 190.245 and rules, and permits the department to adjust initial licensure periods from one to five years to equalize annual renewals.

entries.reviewSummary: Extends existing ambulance vehicle and aircraft licenses for one year after the effective date of sections 190.001 to 190.245, sets an August 28, 1999 compliance deadline, and allows staggered initial licensure periods to equalize renewals.

headings.title: Prohibition on employing or permitting unlicensed personnel
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits employers from knowingly employing or permitting an employee to perform regulated services until the person holds all required licenses, certificates, or authorizations.

headings.title: Employer and supervisor cooperation with compliance monitoring
headings.reviewNote: Requires persons or entities employing or supervising EMRs, dispatchers, EMTs, nurses, PAs, or physicians to cooperate with department compliance monitoring and enforcement.

headings.title: Employer seventy-two-hour reporting of specified felony charges
