headings.reviewNote: Requires employers of department-licensed individuals to report within seventy-two hours of knowledge any charges filed against an employee for felony child abuse or sexual abuse, crimes of violence, or rape or sexual abuse.

headings.title: Licensee seventy-two-hour self-reporting of felony charges
headings.reviewNote: Requires any licensee charged with a felony offense listed in subsection 3 to report the filing of charges to the department within seventy-two hours.

headings.title: Department monitoring for potential licensure action
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the department will monitor felony-charge reports for possible licensure action authorized under section 190.165.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibits employers from permitting unlicensed EMS practice, mandates employer cooperation with department compliance monitoring, requires seventy-two-hour reporting of specified felony charges by employers and licensees, and directs department monitoring for section 190.165 action.

headings.title: Public and professional EMS information and education programs
headings.reviewNote: Permits DHSS, with hospitals and local or regional EMS agencies, to provide public and professional education on EMS, trauma, STEMI, and stroke centers, proper EMS use, CPR, and public emergency care training.

headings.title: Department duties for trauma, STEMI, and stroke transport protocols
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to compile clinical guidelines, assess EMS and hospital capacity, adopt section 190.243 transport protocol rules, define coordination regions, promote community or regional plans, and set plan submission procedures.

headings.title: Approval of community or regional transport plans and rule waivers
headings.reviewNote: Requires community or regional trauma, STEMI, and stroke transport plans developed by hospitals, physicians, and EMS providers to be submitted for department approval with outcome evaluation, waiving inconsistent rules upon approval.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes public and professional EMS education programs, directs the department to compile clinical guidelines, assess capacity, adopt trauma, STEMI, and stroke transport protocols, and governs approval of community-based or regional transport plans with rule waivers.

headings.title: Direct benefit payment to ambulance services and response agencies
headings.reviewNote: Requires health carriers and managed care plans to pay benefits directly to ambulance services or emergency medical response agencies.

headings.title: Prohibition on discouraging 911 emergency system use
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits health carriers and managed care plans from prohibiting or discouraging use of the 911 system when emergency services are needed as defined in section 190.100.

headings.title: Immediate notification of 911 provider upon emergency request
headings.reviewNote: Requires a non-911 ambulance service receiving a request for emergency services to immediately notify the 911 provider or recognized emergency provider.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires health carriers and managed care plans to pay ambulance benefits directly and not discourage 911 use, and mandates immediate notification of the 911 provider when a non-911 ambulance service receives an emergency request.

headings.title: Advance facility notification prior to transporting at-risk patients
headings.reviewNote: Requires licensed hospitals and nursing homes to maintain policies requiring advance notification to EMS personnel before transporting any at-risk behavioral health patient.

headings.title: Permitted EMS training on restraint and de-escalation techniques
headings.reviewNote: Permits licensed EMS personnel conducting interfacility transfers of at-risk behavioral health patients to be trained, as determined by the medical director, in proper restraint and verbal de-escalation techniques.

headings.title: Physician temporary involuntary hold for transport and EMS immunity
headings.reviewNote: Permits an emergency treating physician to place an at-risk behavioral health patient on a temporary involuntary hold for immediate transport (subject to section 632.440) and shields EMS personnel relying on the order from negligence, false imprisonment, and privacy claims.

headings.title: Preservation of federal Mental Health Patient's Bill of Rights
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that this section does not limit patient rights under 42 U.S.C. Section 9501(1)(A) and (F).

headings.title: Definition of at-risk behavioral health patient
headings.reviewNote: Defines at-risk behavioral health patient as any patient who displays violent, homicidal, or suicidal ideation or behavior.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires hospitals and nursing homes to notify EMS before transporting at-risk behavioral health patients, permits EMS restraint and de-escalation training, authorizes physician temporary involuntary holds for transport with EMS immunity, preserves federal patient rights, and defines at-risk behavioral health patient.

headings.title: Designation of adult and pediatric trauma centers
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department, except under subsection 4, to designate qualifying hospitals as adult or pediatric trauma centers upon application and site review (or national verification without site review) using evidence-based guidelines such as American College of Surgeons standards.

headings.title: Designation of STEMI and stroke centers
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department, except under subsection 4, to designate qualifying hospitals as STEMI or stroke centers upon application and site review (or national certification without site review) using ACC, AHA, or ASA guidelines.

headings.title: Triennial site reviews, probation, and revocation for noncompliance
headings.reviewNote: Requires site reviews at least every three years (except subsection 4 centers), authorizes denial, probation (12 months or up to 18 months by settlement), suspension, or revocation for substantial noncompliance, and mandates revocation after two consecutive failed site reviews.

headings.title: Alternative state designation based on national certification
headings.reviewNote: Permits hospitals to obtain corresponding state designation based on national certification without additional standards, allows removal upon request or revoked national certification without judicial review, and requires reporting complaints to the certifying body.

headings.title: Reporting, EMS collaboration, and stroke consultation duties for nationally designated centers
headings.reviewNote: Requires subsection 4 centers to submit proof of certification and leader contacts within thirty days and participate in local/regional EMS systems, and requires level III stroke centers to maintain formal level I or II thrombolytic consultation agreements.

headings.title: State or national registry data submission without duplication
headings.reviewNote: Requires designated centers to submit data to a state or national registry, barring extra data elements or duplicative entry when using a national registry while prohibiting withholding department access.

headings.title: Confidentiality and national conformity of collected center data
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits disclosing health care professional names or patient-identifying data, limits use to evaluating and improving trauma, stroke, and STEMI care, and requires conformity with national registry specifications.

headings.title: Limits on physician and provider education requirements
headings.reviewNote: Bars DHSS from adding education mandates for ABEM- or AOBEM-certified or board-eligible emergency physicians and caps education requirements for other providers at national designating body standards.

headings.title: Survey fees to offset center inspection costs
headings.reviewNote: Permits DHSS to establish appropriate fees solely to offset the costs of trauma, STEMI, and stroke center surveys.

headings.title: Prohibition on unauthorized public holding out as specialty center
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits any hospital from holding itself out to the public as a STEMI, stroke, or adult or pediatric trauma center unless designated by DHSS.

headings.title: Administrative Hearing Commission review of designation actions
headings.reviewNote: Permits any person aggrieved by a DHSS trauma, STEMI, or stroke center designation action to seek chapter 621 AHC determination without exhausting internal department remedies.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs department designation of trauma, STEMI, and stroke centers, triennial site reviews and discipline, alternative national-designation pathways, registry data submission and confidentiality, physician education limits, survey fees, unauthorized holding-out bans, and AHC appeals.

headings.title: Exemption from obtaining EMS data unavailable from state database
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits DHSS rules from requiring hospitals as a section 190.241 designation condition to obtain EMS data unless obtainable from the state EMS database, without limiting EMS data submission duties; source note records original rolls read 'sections'.

headings.title: Relief from inconsistently interpreted specialty center regulations
headings.reviewNote: Relieves a hospital from complying with a trauma, STEMI, or stroke regulation interpretation shown to differ for a similarly situated hospital, while permitting DHSS to require compliance once interpreted consistently.

headings.title: Department attendance at meetings with designated centers
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to attend meetings with trauma, STEMI, and stroke centers to improve communication, identify best practices, and improve the designation process.

headings.title: Definition of hospital incorporating section 197.020
headings.reviewNote: Defines hospital for this section as having the same meaning as in section 197.020.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibits regulations requiring hospitals to obtain EMS data unavailable from the state database, relieves hospitals from inconsistently interpreted trauma, STEMI, or stroke rules, requires DHSS communication meetings, and incorporates the chapter 197 hospital definition.

headings.title: Mandatory transport to designated trauma, STEMI, and stroke centers
headings.reviewNote: Requires severely injured patients to be transported to a trauma center, STEMI patients to a STEMI center, and stroke patients to a stroke center.

headings.title: Verbal medical direction and nearest stabilization facility transport
headings.reviewNote: Requires a verbally communicating physician, PA, or authorized RN to direct transport to the closest hospital or designated center by estimated time even outside the primary service area, and permits transport to the nearest facility for stabilization when initial transport would be prolonged.

headings.title: Clinical appropriateness over reimbursement considerations
headings.reviewNote: Requires transport of STEMI, stroke, or severely injured patients to be governed by timely and medically appropriate care, which reimbursement mechanisms shall not supersede.

headings.title: Hospital of choice for non-qualifying patients
headings.reviewNote: Requires patients not meeting direct specialty-center transport criteria to be transported to the hospital of their choice unless violating local protocols.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates transporting severely injured, STEMI, and stroke patients to designated centers, governs medical direction and stabilization transport outside primary service areas, prioritizes clinical care over reimbursement, and allows hospital of choice for non-critical patients.

headings.title: Definitions for epinephrine delivery systems
headings.reviewNote: Defines eligible person, firm, organization, or entity; emergency health care provider; and epinephrine delivery system for this section.

headings.title: Training, maintenance, and reporting limits on possession and use
headings.reviewNote: Requires director-approved training to use an epinephrine delivery system (except licensed professionals within scope or lawful prescriptions), mandates department-rule maintenance and disposal, and requires immediate reporting of every use to the emergency health care provider.

headings.title: First-aid status, lawful practice protection, and authorized sales
headings.reviewNote: Deems authorized use first aid or emergency treatment for liability laws, clarifies that authorized acquisition, possession, or use is not unlawful practice of medicine or a profession, and permits authorized sellers to supply authorized recipients.

headings.title: Class B misdemeanor penalty for violations
headings.reviewNote: Makes any person, firm, organization, or entity violating this section guilty of a class B misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines terms for epinephrine delivery systems, restricts use to trained persons with professional and prescription exceptions, classifies authorized use as first aid and not unlawful medical practice, and makes violations a class B misdemeanor.

headings.title: Six-month deadline to complete violation investigations
headings.reviewNote: Requires all investigations of alleged violations of sections 190.001 to 190.245 to be completed within six months of receiving the allegation.

headings.title: Department access to directly related licensee records
headings.reviewNote: Grants the department access during an investigation to all records directly related to alleged violations held by persons or entities licensed under chapter 190, 197, or 198.

headings.title: Six-month completion period for multi-agency investigations
headings.reviewNote: Requires department investigations involving other administrative or law enforcement agencies to be completed within six months after notification and final determination by those agencies.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires EMS violation investigations to be completed within six months, grants department access to directly related licensee records, and sets a six-month completion period following external agency determinations.

headings.title: Definitions for ambulance service statutory liens
headings.reviewNote: Defines claim, insurance carrier, and patient for this section.

headings.title: Grant of hospital statutory lien rights to ambulance services
headings.reviewNote: Grants ambulance services the same statutory lien rights granted to hospitals in sections 430.230 to 430.250.

headings.title: Proportional sharing up to fifty percent of net proceeds
headings.reviewNote: Requires ambulance services and hospitals giving notice to share proportionally in up to fifty percent of net proceeds (after contractual attorney fees and recovery expenses) when combined liens exceed fifty percent of the amount due the patient.

headings.title: Direct payment of lien by insurance carrier
headings.reviewNote: Permits an insurance carrier administering an ambulance service lien to pay the secured amount directly if authorized by the claimant without disputing customary charges or causation.

headings.title: Release of claimant from further liability upon receipt of benefits
headings.reviewNote: Provides that an ambulance service electing to receive benefits under this section releases the claimant from further liability for the cost of services and treatment provided to that point.

entries.reviewSummary: Grants ambulance services the same statutory lien rights as hospitals under sections 430.230 to 430.250, defines terms, caps combined liens at fifty percent of net proceeds, permits direct insurer payment, and releases claimants upon acceptance.

headings.title: First responder authority to obtain and administer opioid overdose drugs
headings.reviewNote: Permits any qualified first responder to obtain and administer naloxone or other FDA-approved opioid overdose-blocking drugs or devices in an FDA-approved manner to revive an apparent overdose victim.

headings.title: Authorized sales by Missouri drug distributors and pharmacies
headings.reviewNote: Permits licensed Missouri drug distributors and pharmacies to sell naloxone or other FDA-approved opioid overdose drugs or devices to qualified first responder agencies to stock for emergency administration.

headings.title: Definitions of qualified first responder and agency
headings.reviewNote: Defines qualified first responder (trained fire, EMT under local medical director protocols, or state/local law enforcement personnel) and qualified first responder agencies (agencies providing documented overdose training).

headings.title: Administration limited to trained methods
headings.reviewNote: Restricts a qualified first responder to administering naloxone or other FDA-approved opioid overdose drugs or devices only by means for which the responder has received training.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes qualified first responders to obtain and administer FDA-approved opioid overdose drugs or devices, permits Missouri drug distributors and pharmacies to sell them to qualified agencies, defines terms, and limits administration to trained methods.

headings.title: Establishment and advisory duties of Time-Critical Diagnosis Advisory Committee
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Time-Critical Diagnosis Advisory Committee designated by the director to advise DHSS on education, cooperative research, standards, protocols, state regulations, and community or regional plans.

headings.title: Uncompensated service and budgeted expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Provides that committee members serve without compensation, except that the department shall budget for reasonable travel and meeting expenses.

headings.title: Sixteen-member EMS and hospital composition
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to appoint sixteen members from applications, consisting of six EMS region participants (including a regional medical director, air ambulance, urban, and rural members) and ten hospital representatives (including trauma, STEMI, stroke, rural/critical access, and three physicians).

headings.title: Ex officio membership of state EMS medical director
headings.reviewNote: Designates the state EMS medical director as an ex officio member of the committee in addition to the sixteen appointees.

headings.title: Geographical representation across hospital association districts
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to make a reasonable effort to ensure hospital-representing members have geographical representation from each state district designated by a statewide nonprofit hospital association.

headings.title: Three-year staggered terms and reapplication requirement
headings.reviewNote: Sets three-year terms with extended initial terms so roughly one-third expire annually, and requires appointees wishing to continue to resubmit an application.

headings.title: Consultation with state EMS advisory council
headings.reviewNote: Requires the committee to consult with the state advisory council on emergency medical services under section 190.101 regarding emergency medical services issues.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the sixteen-member Time-Critical Diagnosis Advisory Committee, defines its advisory duties, expense reimbursement, EMS and hospital membership, ex officio state EMS medical director, geographic balance, three-year staggered terms, and consultation with the state EMS advisory council.

headings.title: Short title of First Informer Broadcasters Act
headings.reviewNote: Provides that this section shall be known and may be cited as the First Informer Broadcasters Act.

headings.title: Definitions of broadcaster and first informer broadcaster
headings.reviewNote: Defines broadcaster (FCC-licensed radio or TV station participating in the Emergency Alert System) and first informer broadcaster (certified under this section).

headings.title: DPS training and statewide credentialing program for broadcast personnel
headings.reviewNote: Directs the Department of Public Safety, with a statewide broadcasters organization, to establish a training and statewide credentialing program covering disaster facility restoration and personal safety.

headings.title: Disaster-area access to restore and resupply broadcast equipment
headings.reviewNote: Requires state and local agencies, to the extent practicable without endangering public safety or recovery, to grant certified first informer broadcasters disaster-area access to restore, repair, or resupply critical broadcast equipment and generators.

headings.title: Association responsibility for training program costs
headings.reviewNote: Requires the statewide association involved in establishing the program to pay the costs of developing and implementing the training program.

entries.reviewSummary: Enacts the First Informer Broadcasters Act, defining broadcaster terms, directing a Department of Public Safety training and credentialing program, granting disaster-area access to restore broadcast facilities, and assigning program costs to the participating statewide association.

headings.title: Prohibition on rules requiring hospital helipad fencing or barriers
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits DHSS rules under chapters 190, 192, 197, or other Missouri law from requiring fencing or barriers around hospital helipads and declares any such regulation or interpretation null and void.

headings.title: Prohibition on department rules for helipad operation or construction
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits the department from promulgating any rules and regulations regarding the operation or construction of a helipad located at a hospital.

headings.title: Hospital duty to keep helipads unobstructed and safe
headings.reviewNote: Requires hospitals to ensure that helipads are free of obstruction and safe for helicopter use on the ground and during approach and takeoff.

headings.title: Definition of hospital incorporating section 197.020
headings.reviewNote: Defines hospital for this section as having the same meaning as in section 197.020.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibits DHSS regulations requiring fencing or barriers around hospital helipads or regulating helipad construction or operation, requires hospitals to keep helipads unobstructed and safe, and incorporates the section 197.020 hospital definition.

headings.title: Business exemption from state registration, income tax, and use tax
headings.reviewNote: Provides that out-of-state businesses repairing or building declared-disaster infrastructure during a disaster period do not establish presence triggering secretary of state registration (except section 190.285), income/withholding taxes, or use tax on equipment removed after the period.

headings.title: Tax residency and withholding exemption for out-of-state employees
headings.reviewNote: Provides that out-of-state employees performing disaster infrastructure work during a disaster period do not establish residency or presence triggering state or local income or withholding taxes or fees.

headings.title: Applicability of standard requirements after disaster period
headings.reviewNote: Subjects out-of-state businesses or employees remaining in Missouri after a disaster period concludes to all state or local employment, licensing, and registration requirements suspended under sections 190.270 to 190.285.

entries.reviewSummary: Exempts out-of-state businesses and employees repairing declared-disaster infrastructure during a disaster period from specified state and local registration, income tax, withholding, and temporary equipment use tax requirements, ending after the disaster period.

headings.title: Ten-day notification to secretary of state upon disaster entry
headings.reviewNote: Requires an out-of-state business responding to a declared disaster to notify the secretary of state within ten days of entry with its name, domicile, principal address, FEIN, entry date, and in-state contact information.

headings.title: Affiliate notification by registered in-state businesses
headings.reviewNote: Requires a registered business to provide the subsection 1 notification for an out-of-state affiliate entering the state, including the registered business's in-state contact information.

headings.title: Post-disaster notification and compliance if remaining in state
headings.reviewNote: Requires an out-of-state business remaining after a disaster period to notify the secretary of state within ten days after the period ends and meet all resulting registration, licensing, and filing requirements.

headings.title: Transmission of notifications to department of revenue
headings.reviewNote: Requires the secretary of state to provide received disaster business notifications to the department of revenue within thirty days of receipt.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires out-of-state disaster response businesses and registered affiliates to notify the secretary of state within ten days of entry and post-disaster retention, and requires forwarding notifications to the department of revenue within thirty days.

headings.title: Emergency services sales tax authorization
headings.reviewNote: Permits the county commission, in lieu of a section 190.305 levy, to impose a county sales tax for central dispatching of emergency services, including communications and emergency equipment and operational costs.

headings.title: Submission of proposal by commission vote or voter petition
headings.reviewNote: Permits the county commission by majority vote to submit the sales tax proposal to voters and requires submission upon a voter petition signed by ten percent of the last gubernatorial vote.

headings.title: Prescribed ballot language and effect of vote
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes the ballot form for the county emergency services sales tax, making the ordinance effective upon majority approval and barring imposition upon rejection unless resubmitted and approved.

headings.title: One percent rate cap and pre-operation collection limit
headings.reviewNote: Caps the sales tax at one percent on taxable retail sales under sections 144.010 to 144.525 and prohibits collection more than thirty-six months before central dispatching begins operating.

headings.title: Applicability of local sales tax administration statutes
headings.reviewNote: Applies sections 32.085 and 32.087 to the sales tax imposed under this section except as modified herein.

headings.title: Termination of section 190.305 telephone tax upon operation
headings.reviewNote: Terminates any section 190.305 tax at the end of the tax year in which the board certifies this section's tax is fully operational, crediting prior revenues to their intended purposes.

headings.title: Annual board tax rate determination and retailer notice
headings.reviewNote: Requires the board annually by September first to set a rate within the authorized cap balancing expenditures and carried-forward surplus, publish it in its minutes, and notify every retailer by mail.

headings.title: Appointment of initial board, election transition, and relinquishment
headings.reviewNote: Requires immediate county commission appointment of an initial emergency services board upon voter approval, transitions to elected boards beginning in 1994, and requires the commission to relinquish chapter 190 emergency service duties.

headings.title: Composition and geographic representation of initial board
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a seven-member nonpartisan initial board (three representing emergency services/municipalities and four not), grandfathers members serving August 28, 2004, and limits appointments to four per commission district.

headings.title: Elected board districts, chair, staggered terms, and election date
headings.reviewNote: Provides beginning in 1994 for electing three members per commission district and one at-large member at the first municipal election of the year, with annual chair election, staggered initial terms, and four-year terms from 1996.

headings.title: Corporate status and name of emergency services board
headings.reviewNote: Declares the organized board to be a body corporate and political subdivision of the state known as the Emergency Services Board.

headings.title: County population applicability restriction
headings.reviewNote: Limits this section to third-class non-township counties with more than 24,500 and fewer than 24,600 inhabitants.

headings.title: Exemption for prepaid wireless telecommunications service
headings.reviewNote: Exempts purchases providing prepaid wireless telecommunications service from this section or section 190.335 taxes unless the county prohibited the section 190.460 charge without subsequently voting to impose it.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes a county emergency services sales tax up to one percent in Warren County in lieu of section 190.305 levies, prescribes ballot language, annual rate setting, initial appointed and elected seven-member Emergency Services Board governance, corporate status, and a prepaid wireless exemption.

headings.title: Enumerated powers and duties of emergency services board
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates sixteen board powers and duties including 911 planning, receiving sales tax funds, staffing, land acquisition, borrowing and bonding, suing, contracting, benefits, bylaws, equal service, and liability insurance without waiving immunity.

headings.title: Sole administrative control over tax moneys and central dispatch
headings.reviewNote: Vests administrative control and management of section 190.292 sales tax moneys and central dispatching solely in the board, including hiring personnel, setting pay, and providing quarters and equipment.

headings.title: Authority to contract for central dispatching services
headings.reviewNote: Permits the board to contract for services relating in whole or part to central dispatching of emergency services and expend tax or other funds therefor.

headings.title: Election of officers and treasurer surety bond
headings.reviewNote: Requires the board to elect a vice chairman, treasurer, secretary, and other officers, and requires the treasurer before taking office to furnish a board-paid Missouri-authorized surety bond.

headings.title: Acceptance of gifts and exclusive control over board funds
headings.reviewNote: Permits the board to accept, sell, or exchange gifts of property or money for central dispatch and vests exclusive control over gifts, investment proceeds, tax revenues, and government grants or loans.

headings.title: Grounds and vote for removal of board members
headings.reviewNote: Permits removal of a board member after notice and hearing by majority vote of the other members for missing five consecutive meetings without good cause, prejudicial conduct, or neglect of duty.

headings.title: Presiding officer and procedures at removal hearings
headings.reviewNote: Designates the chairperson (or another elected member if the chair is the subject) to preside at removal hearings with sworn witnesses, party testimony and arguments, and optional recording at a party's expense.

headings.title: Filling of board vacancies until next election
headings.reviewNote: Requires remaining board members to fill vacancies caused by removal, resignation, or otherwise, with appointees serving until the next director election for the unexpired term.

headings.title: Twelve-month post-service employment prohibition
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits individual board members from being employed by the board within twelve months of terminating board service.

headings.title: Fourth-degree nepotism prohibition
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits the board from employing any person related within the fourth degree by blood or marriage to any board member.

headings.title: Chapter 536 rulemaking compliance and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Subjects rules created under sections 190.300 to 190.341 to chapter 536 and section 536.028 and declares nonseverability for rules after August 28, 2004; Revisor's Note records section 190.341 does not exist.

headings.title: County population applicability restriction
headings.reviewNote: Limits this section to third-class non-township counties with more than 24,500 and fewer than 24,600 inhabitants.

entries.reviewSummary: Enumerates powers and duties of the Warren County Emergency Services Board, grants sole administrative control over tax funds and dispatch, governs officers, gifts, member removal hearings, vacancies, employment and nepotism bars, chapter 536 rulemaking, and county applicability.

headings.title: Authority to borrow money and issue bonds upon voter approval
headings.reviewNote: Permits the emergency services board to borrow money and issue bonds to purchase central dispatch property or equipment, submitted to county voters at the first municipal election of a calendar year.

headings.title: Prescribed ballot form for bond proposition
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes the substantially required ballot question form for submitting an emergency services board bond borrowing proposition.

headings.title: Board bonding power upon constitutionally required vote
headings.reviewNote: Vests the board, upon approval by the constitutionally required percentage of votes cast and subject to subsection 4, with power to borrow and issue bonds for the ballot-specified amount and purposes.

headings.title: Term, debt cap, interest limit, and sinking fund directive
headings.reviewNote: Limits loans to twenty years, caps aggregate debt at ten percent of taxable tangible property value, caps interest at the highest legal contract rate, and requires directing section 190.292 tax revenue to pay interest and fund a sinking fund.

headings.title: County population applicability restriction
headings.reviewNote: Limits this section to third-class non-township counties with more than 24,500 and fewer than 24,600 inhabitants.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes the Warren County Emergency Services Board to borrow money and issue bonds for central dispatch property or equipment upon voter approval, prescribes ballot language, sets twenty-year and ten-percent debt limits with sinking fund duties, and restricts applicability by county population.

headings.title: Emergency telephone service tax authorization and county contracting rules
headings.reviewNote: Permits governing bodies to provide emergency telephone service funded by a tax up to fifteen percent of the tariff local service rate or seventy-five cents per line per month, and sets special contracting and board rules for qualifying counties.

headings.title: Permitted operational uses and pre-operation collection window
headings.reviewNote: Directs tax use for emergency telephone service and call answering/dispatching operational costs, permitting levy after contract execution but barring collection more than twenty-seven months before operations begin.

headings.title: Tariff-rate limitation and one-hundred-line cap
headings.reviewNote: Limits the tax to the tariff rate and prohibits imposing it on more than one hundred exchange access facilities or their equivalent per person per location.

headings.title: Liability of billed service users for tax
headings.reviewNote: Makes every billed service user liable for the emergency telephone tax until it has been paid to the service supplier.

headings.title: Commencement of supplier collection duty and separate billing
headings.reviewNote: Begins the service supplier's collection duty at the time specified by the governing body and requires adding the tax to billings, where it may be stated separately.

headings.title: No supplier duty to sue and reporting of unpaid users
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that service suppliers are not obligated to take legal action to enforce collection, but requires providing the governing body a list of uncollected amounts and refusing users' names and addresses.

headings.title: Collection with regular billing and tariff rate presumption
headings.reviewNote: Requires collecting the tax insofar as practicable alongside regular tariff billings and establishes a rebuttable presumption that supplier-billed tariff rates made under business practices are correct.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes local governing bodies to levy an emergency telephone tax up to fifteen percent of the tariff rate or seventy-five cents per line, addresses Christian and Scott County contracting, sets operational uses, 100-line caps, user liability, billing collection, and rate presumptions.

headings.title: Civil immunity for public agencies operating emergency systems
headings.reviewNote: Shields public agencies, public safety agencies, and their officers, agents, and employees from civil damages for developing, adopting, operating, or implementing a section 190.300 to 190.340 plan or system, except for willful and wanton misconduct or gross negligence.

headings.title: Civil immunity for giving or following emergency instructions
headings.reviewNote: Shields persons giving or following emergency instructions through a section 190.300 to 190.340 system for remote emergency services from civil damages, unless constituting willful and wanton misconduct or gross negligence.

headings.title: Preservation of sovereign, official, and public duty immunities
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that nothing in this section abrogates any immunity existing in its absence, including sovereign immunity, official immunity, or the public duty doctrine.

entries.reviewSummary: Grants qualified civil immunity for operating 911 emergency systems and giving or following emergency instructions under sections 190.300 to 190.340 except for willful and wanton misconduct or gross negligence, while preserving existing governmental immunities.

headings.title: Prohibition on misuse of 911 emergency telephone service and definitions
headings.reviewNote: Makes misusing county 911 emergency telephone service unlawful and defines emergency, misuse (including repeatedly calling 911 for nonemergencies), and repeatedly (three or more times in one month).

headings.title: Class B misdemeanor criminal penalty
headings.reviewNote: Provides that any violation of this section is a class B misdemeanor.

headings.title: Prohibition on local fines for pay telephone 911 calls
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits political subdivisions from imposing fines or penalties on pay telephone owners or property owners for 911 calls made from a pay telephone and declares any such fine or penalty void.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibits misuse of county 911 emergency telephone services including repeated nonemergency calls, makes violations a class B misdemeanor, and voids local fines or penalties on pay telephone owners for 911 calls.

headings.title: Authorization and general powers of county 911 board
headings.reviewNote: Permits any county to establish an Emergency Telephone Service 911 Board with county-defined powers including 911 planning, system implementation and upgrades, receiving and disbursing section 190.305 tax moneys, and hiring staff.

headings.title: Appointment, eleven-member composition, terms, and expenses
headings.reviewNote: Directs the county governing body to appoint eleven board members (at least six public safety representatives, or seven named officials in a specified third-class county) for staggered initial and three-year terms without compensation but with expense reimbursement.

headings.title: Sole administrative control, personnel, and LAGERS eligibility
headings.reviewNote: Vests sole administrative control of county 911 service in the board to employ personnel, set pay, and provide quarters and equipment, making board employees eligible for LAGERS under sections 70.600 to 70.755.

headings.title: Authority to contract for emergency telephone 911 services
headings.reviewNote: Permits the board to contract for services relating in whole or part to emergency telephone 911 service and expend tax or other funds therefor.

headings.title: Election of board officers and treasurer surety bond
headings.reviewNote: Requires the board to elect a chairman, vice chairman, treasurer, and other officers, and requires the treasurer before taking office to furnish a board-paid Missouri-authorized surety bond.

headings.title: Board rulemaking for 911 system establishment and operation
headings.reviewNote: Requires the board to set rules for establishing and operating the emergency 911 system and do all other things necessary to carry out sections 190.300 to 190.320.

headings.title: Authority to contract with not-for-profit corporations
headings.reviewNote: Permits the board to contract with any not-for-profit corporation, including one incorporated to implement sections 190.300 to 190.320.

headings.title: Acceptance of gifts and exclusive control over board funds
headings.reviewNote: Permits the board to accept, sell, or exchange gifts of property or money for county 911 service and vests exclusive control over gifts, investment proceeds, county 911 tax revenues, and government grants or loans.

headings.title: Grounds and vote for removal of board members
headings.reviewNote: Permits removal of a board member after notice and hearing by majority vote of the other members for missing five consecutive meetings without good cause, prejudicial conduct, or neglect of duty.

headings.title: Presiding officer and procedures at removal hearings
headings.reviewNote: Designates the chairman (or another elected member if the chairman is the subject) to preside at removal hearings with sworn witnesses, party testimony and arguments, and optional recording at a party's expense.

headings.title: Reporting and filling of board vacancies
headings.reviewNote: Requires the board chairman to report vacancies to the county governing body to be filled like original appointments, with unexpired-term appointments limited to the remainder of the term.

headings.title: Twelve-month post-service employment prohibition
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits individual board members from being employed by the board within twelve months of terminating board service.

headings.title: Fourth-degree nepotism prohibition
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits the board from employing any person related within the fourth degree of consanguinity or affinity to any board member.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes county Emergency Telephone Service 911 Boards, governing their eleven-member composition, sole administrative control and LAGERS eligibility, contracting, officers, rules, gifts, member removal hearings, vacancies, twelve-month post-service employment bar, and fourth-degree nepotism prohibition.

headings.title: Quarterly remittance, return filing, and one-year record retention
headings.reviewNote: Makes section 190.300 to 190.320 taxes due quarterly with remittance and agreed-form returns (including refusing users) due within sixty days after quarter close, and requires retaining records for one year.

headings.title: Two-percent supplier collection fee for timely remittance
headings.reviewNote: Entitles a service supplier to deduct and retain a two-percent collection fee from every remittance made on or before the due date.

headings.title: Annual tax rate determination, surplus carryover, notice, and audits
headings.reviewNote: Requires the governing body annually by September first to set a rate balancing expenditures and carried-forward surplus, publish it in minutes, notify registered suppliers by mail, and permits auditing supplier tax records.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes quarterly remittance, return filing, and one-year record retention for emergency telephone taxes, grants suppliers a two-percent timely collection fee, and requires annual rate setting by September first with audit authority.

headings.title: Use of emergency telephone taxes and 911 charges in specified counties
headings.reviewNote: Permits qualifying county commissions to use section 190.305 emergency telephone taxes for central dispatching and equipment, and permits specified charter counties to use section 190.460 charges for public safety capital improvements.

headings.title: Monthly $1.30 per-line rate cap, returns, retention, and collection fee
headings.reviewNote: Caps the tax at $1.30 per line per month, requires monthly returns and remittances within one month with one-year record retention, and grants a two-percent timely collection fee; source note records 'and' is absent from original rolls.

headings.title: Voluntary municipal participation and contracting with dispatch board
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that no municipality or political subdivision is required to join central dispatching and permits contracting with the section 190.327 board for services or equipment.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes specified Clay, Jackson, and Jefferson County commissions to use emergency telephone taxes for central dispatching and section 190.460 charges for public safety capital improvements, caps monthly taxes at $1.30 per line with a two-percent fee, and makes municipal participation voluntary by contract.

headings.title: Initial board appointment, elections, and commission relinquishment
headings.reviewNote: Requires county commission appointment of an initial central dispatch board upon voting to use telephone taxes for central dispatch, transitions to elected boards beginning in 1992, and relinquishes chapter 190 and 321 dispatch duties to the board.

headings.title: Option for board elections on general municipal election day
headings.reviewNote: Permits board member elections to be held on general municipal election day under section 115.121(3) upon simple majority approval by the county commission.

headings.title: Enumerated corporate powers of central dispatch board
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates ten board powers including corporate seal, suing, contracting, acquiring or encumbering property, managing improvements, hiring with benefits, adopting bylaws, collecting taxes and fees, and paying election expenses.

headings.title: Alternative seven-member appointed board upon local request
headings.reviewNote: Permits the county commission, upon municipal and political subdivision request, to appoint a seven-member board (five ex officio sheriff/police/fire heads and two two-year district/department heads) exercising subsection 3 powers.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs appointment and subsequent election of central dispatch boards with county commission duty relinquishment, permits municipal election day voting, enumerates corporate powers, and authorizes an alternative seven-member appointed board.

headings.title: Initial township board composition and at-large chairperson
headings.reviewNote: Establishes an initial board beginning in 1997 in qualifying non-Mississippi-bordering third-class county areas with two members per township and one at-large chairperson.

headings.title: Voter election of township and at-large dispatch board members
headings.reviewNote: Requires voters in qualifying third-class county central dispatch areas to elect two members from each township and one at-large member serving as board chairperson.

headings.title: Staggered terms, four-year successors, and consolidation termination
headings.reviewNote: Sets staggered two- and four-year initial terms and four-year subsequent terms, ending existing terms thirty days after initial board appointment upon section 190.470 consolidation.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs initial and elected township-based central dispatch boards in specified Christian and Scott County areas, staggered two- and four-year terms, and early term termination upon section 190.470 consolidation.

headings.title: Initial seven-member appointed board and geographic balance
headings.reviewNote: Requires appointing a seven-member nonpartisan initial board representing emergency services and the public (outside exempted third-class county areas), with no more than four members from any commission district.

headings.title: Elected board districts, terms, vacancies, quorum, and consolidation
headings.reviewNote: Provides beginning in 1992 for electing three members per commission district and an at-large voting chair, sets staggered and four-year terms, four-member quorum, appointment for vacancies, and 30-day term end upon section 190.470 consolidation.

headings.title: Seven-month term reduction upon moving to municipal election day
headings.reviewNote: Reduces sitting board members' terms by seven months upon county commission approval of general municipal election day voting under section 190.327(2), with four-year terms thereafter.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs initial seven-member appointed boards and successor elected commission-district boards for central dispatching outside exempted areas, sets staggered and four-year terms, quorum, vacancies, consolidation expiration, and seven-month term reductions when moving to municipal election day.

headings.title: County sales tax authorization for central dispatching
headings.reviewNote: Permits any county commission, in lieu of a section 190.305 levy, to impose a county sales tax for central dispatching of emergency services, including communications and emergency equipment and operational costs.

headings.title: Submission of proposal by commission vote or voter petition
headings.reviewNote: Permits the county commission by majority vote to submit the sales tax proposal to voters and requires submission upon a voter petition signed by ten percent of the last gubernatorial vote.

headings.title: Prescribed ballot language and effect of vote
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes the ballot form for the county central dispatch sales tax, making the ordinance effective upon majority approval and barring imposition upon rejection unless resubmitted and approved.

headings.title: One percent rate cap and pre-operation collection limit
headings.reviewNote: Caps the sales tax at one percent on taxable retail sales under sections 144.010 to 144.525 and prohibits collection more than thirty-six months before central dispatching begins operating.

headings.title: Applicability of local sales tax administration statutes
headings.reviewNote: Applies sections 32.085 and 32.087 to the sales tax imposed under this section except as modified herein.

headings.title: Termination of section 190.305 telephone tax upon operation
headings.reviewNote: Terminates any section 190.305 tax at the end of the tax year in which the board certifies this section's tax is fully operational, crediting prior revenues to their intended purposes.

headings.title: Annual board tax rate determination and retailer notice
headings.reviewNote: Requires the board annually by September first to set a rate within the authorized cap balancing expenditures and carried-forward surplus, publish it in its minutes, and notify every retailer by mail.

headings.title: Appointment of initial board, election transition, and relinquishment
headings.reviewNote: Requires immediate county commission appointment of an initial board upon voter approval, transitions to elected boards beginning in 1994, and requires the commission to relinquish chapter 190 emergency service duties.

headings.title: Composition and geographic representation of initial board
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a seven-member nonpartisan initial board representing emergency services and the general public, with no more than four members appointed from each county commission district.

headings.title: Elected board districts, terms, consolidation, and uncontested seats
headings.reviewNote: Provides beginning in 1994 for electing three members per commission district and an at-large chair, sets staggered and four-year terms, ends terms 30 days after section 190.470 consolidation, and cancels elections for uncontested or vacant seats.

headings.title: Continuation and optional reclassification of pre-existing 911 boards
headings.reviewNote: Continues existing section 190.309 boards in specified Greene, Lawrence, and Stoddard county classes with section 190.339 powers, excluding pre-August 25, 2010 boards from political subdivision status unless reclassified by unanimous county commission order.

headings.title: Appointed seven-member board in specified counties
headings.reviewNote: Directs the county commission in specified Christian, Taney, and St. Francois county classes to appoint a seven-member board of emergency service heads (with two public members in a specified county class) exercising section 190.339 powers.

headings.title: Cap on resubmitted tax after pre-2012 automatic reduction
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits any county whose pre-January 1, 2012 levy was automatically reduced after approval from submitting a new proposal exceeding the reduced amount.

headings.title: Exemption for prepaid wireless telecommunications service
headings.reviewNote: Exempts purchases providing prepaid wireless telecommunications service from this section or section 190.292 taxes unless the county prohibited the section 190.460 charge without subsequently voting to impose it.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes county central dispatch sales taxes up to one percent in lieu of section 190.305 levies, prescribes ballot language, annual rate setting, board appointment and election, county-specific board continuation and appointment rules, levy reduction caps, and a prepaid wireless exemption.

headings.title: Subjection to recall and commencement of proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Makes each section 190.335 emergency services board member subject to recall by registered voters of the election district and permits commencing proceedings by filing a notice of intention.

headings.title: Restrictions on timing and frequency of recall proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Bars commencing recall proceedings if the member has served 180 days or less of the current term, has 180 days or less remaining, or won a recall election during the current term.

headings.title: Service, filing, and contents of notice of intention
headings.reviewNote: Requires serving the notice of intention on the board member, filing it with an affidavit of service with the election authority, and including the member's name, up to 200-word grounds statement, and one to five proponents.

headings.title: Board member written answer to recall statement
headings.reviewNote: Permits the board member within seven days to file and serve a written answer up to 200 words for voter information, providing that statement insufficiencies do not invalidate proceedings.

headings.title: Required contents of recall petition before signing
headings.reviewNote: Requires a recall petition, before any signature is affixed, to include a successor election request, the notice of intention and grounds, the member's answer or a statement of no answer, and signer fields.

headings.title: Affidavit of petition circulator
headings.reviewNote: Requires each submitted petition section to include a signed circulator affidavit stating the circulator's name, address, observation of signatures, belief in genuineness, voter registration in the district, and signature dates.

headings.title: Filing deadline for recall petition
headings.reviewNote: Requires filing the recall petition with the election authority within one hundred eighty days after filing the notice of intention.

headings.title: Required number of qualified signatures
headings.reviewNote: Requires qualified signatures equal to at least twenty-five percent of the votes cast in the most recent gubernatorial election in the election district.

headings.title: Verification and certification by election authority
headings.reviewNote: Requires the election authority within twenty days of filing to determine signature sufficiency, file a certificate of examination results, and provide a copy to proponents upon request.

headings.title: Supplementation of insufficient recall petition
headings.reviewNote: Permits supplementing an insufficient petition within ten days of certification and requires the election authority to certify sufficiency of the supplemented petition within ten days.

headings.title: Effect of insufficient supplemented petition
headings.reviewNote: Provides that no action shall be taken if the supplemented petition remains insufficient, though the petition shall remain on file.

headings.title: Submission and contents of sufficiency certificate to board
headings.reviewNote: Requires the election authority to submit a sufficiency certificate to the emergency services board prior to its next meeting stating the member's name and required, total, and valid signature counts.

headings.title: Order of recall election and candidate nominations
headings.reviewNote: Requires the election authority, after board receipt of the certificate, to order a section 115.123 election between 45 and 120 days from receipt and governs nominations by statement of candidacy.

headings.title: Resignation of member prior to recall election
headings.reviewNote: Permits the member to resign at any time prior to forty-two days before the election, removing the recall question from the ballot, declaring the office vacant, and barring the resigning member from filling it.

headings.title: Applicability of chapter 115 and election costs
headings.reviewNote: Applies chapter 115 election conduct and cost payment provisions where appropriate to recall elections under this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes recall procedures for section 190.335 emergency services board members, including timing bars, notice of intention, seven-day member answer, petition contents, circulator affidavits, signature verification, resignation, and chapter 115 elections; source notes record a 2014 veto override for S.B. 593.

headings.title: Permanence of sales tax and voter petition to continue or terminate
headings.reviewNote: Declares section 190.335 sales taxes permanent and restricted to collected purposes, and requires the county commission to submit continuation or termination to voters upon a petition of ten percent of the last gubernatorial vote.

headings.title: Prescribed ballot form for continuation or termination
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes the required ballot form asking voters whether the county shall continue to impose the emergency services sales tax.

headings.title: Effect of continuation or termination vote and board discharge
headings.reviewNote: Continues the tax upon majority YES vote, or upon majority NO vote declares termination effective the first day of the second calendar quarter after revenue director notice, discharges the board, and voids board orders.

headings.title: Termination of services and reestablishment under section 190.305
headings.reviewNote: Deems emergency services terminated upon a majority NO vote under subsection 3 and permits reestablishing them under section 190.305.

entries.reviewSummary: Declares section 190.335 county emergency services sales taxes permanent and dedicated, establishes a ten-percent voter petition and ballot form to continue or terminate the tax, governs repeal effective dates and board discharge, and allows reestablishment under section 190.305.

headings.title: General powers and duties of emergency services board
headings.reviewNote: Includes planning a 911 and dispatching system, supervising implementation and upgrades, receiving and disbursing section 190.335 sales tax moneys, and hiring necessary staff.

headings.title: Body corporate and political subdivision status
headings.reviewNote: Declares the board a body corporate and political subdivision known as the Emergency Services Board, except pre-August 25, 2010 boards operating under section 190.335(11).

headings.title: Sole administrative control over tax moneys and central dispatch
headings.reviewNote: Vests administrative control and management of section 190.335 sales tax moneys and central dispatching solely in the board, including hiring personnel, setting pay, and providing quarters and equipment.

headings.title: Authority to contract for central dispatching services
headings.reviewNote: Permits the board to contract for services relating in whole or part to central dispatching of emergency services and expend tax or other funds therefor.

headings.title: Election of officers and treasurer surety bond
headings.reviewNote: Requires the board to elect a vice chairman, treasurer, secretary, and other officers, and requires the treasurer before taking office to furnish a board-paid Missouri-authorized surety bond.

headings.title: Acceptance of gifts and exclusive control over board funds
headings.reviewNote: Permits the board to accept, sell, or exchange gifts of property or money for central dispatch and vests exclusive control over gifts, investment proceeds, county tax revenues, and government grants or loans.

headings.title: Grounds and vote for removal of board members
headings.reviewNote: Permits removal of a board member after notice and hearing by majority vote of the other members for missing five consecutive meetings without good cause, prejudicial conduct, or neglect of duty.

headings.title: Presiding officer and procedures at removal hearings
headings.reviewNote: Designates the chairperson (or another elected member if the chair is the subject) to preside at removal hearings with sworn witnesses, party testimony and arguments, and optional recording at a party's expense.

headings.title: Filling of board vacancies until next election
headings.reviewNote: Requires remaining board members to fill vacancies caused by removal, resignation, or otherwise, with appointees serving until the next director election for the unexpired term.

headings.title: Twelve-month post-service employment prohibition
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits individual board members from being employed by the board within twelve months of terminating board service.

headings.title: Fourth-degree nepotism prohibition
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits the board from employing any person related within the fourth degree by blood or marriage to any board member.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes powers and duties of section 190.335 emergency services boards, corporate status with pre-August 25, 2010 exception, sole administrative control, contracting, officers and treasurer bond, gifts and funds control, member removal hearings, vacancies, twelve-month post-service employment bar, and fourth-degree nepotism bar.

headings.title: Duties of chairperson and vice chairperson
headings.reviewNote: Requires the chairperson to preside at meetings, act as official board head, and execute required contracts, with the vice chairperson assuming duties during the chairperson's absence or disability.

headings.title: Duties of board secretary
headings.reviewNote: Requires the secretary to keep official meeting records, attest official documents with the board seal, make requested reports, attend meetings, and perform duties imposed by sections 190.335 to 190.342 and board rules.

headings.title: Duties of board treasurer as fund custodian
headings.reviewNote: Designates the treasurer as custodian of board funds, paying money out of the treasury only upon valid checks or drafts.

headings.title: Board authority to adopt additional officer rules
headings.reviewNote: Permits the board from time to time to provide additional rules and regulations concerning officer duties.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines the official duties of the emergency services board chairperson, vice chairperson, secretary, and treasurer, and authorizes additional board rules governing officer duties.

headings.title: Establishment of regional poison information center and network
headings.reviewNote: Requires DHSS to establish a certified Missouri Regional Poison Information Center based on demonstrated ability and AAPCC certification, determine its region, and establish a statewide Missouri Poison Control Network.

headings.title: Required services of Missouri Regional Poison Information Center
headings.reviewNote: Requires the center to provide a physician-supervised 24-hour toll-free referral service, public and professional education, agency cooperation plans, exposure data collection and evaluation, and coordination of poison centers.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs the Department of Health and Senior Services to establish the Missouri Regional Poison Information Center and Missouri Poison Control Network, and specifies required 24-hour referral, education, cooperation, data, and coordination services.

headings.title: Definitions for 911 communications service statutes
headings.reviewNote: Defines active telephone number, communications service (excluding broadband internet and unsubscribed built-in vehicle devices), provider, public safety agency, public safety answering point, subscriber, and wireless service provider.

headings.title: State agency interoperability service agreements for shared radio systems
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes DPS, Highway Patrol, DNR, SEMA, Conservation, and state-owned radio systems, upon local agency or jurisdiction request, to enter interoperability agreements for shared radio frequencies or talk groups.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines key 911 communications service terms for sections 190.400 to 190.460 and authorizes specified state agencies and radio systems to enter interoperability service agreements upon local request.

headings.title: Establishment of Missouri 911 Service Trust Fund and fee remittance
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Missouri 911 Service Trust Fund as a special trust fund and requires all fees collected under sections 190.400 to 190.460 to be remitted to the director of revenue.

headings.title: Deposit and reimbursement uses for 911 operations
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director of revenue to deposit payments into the trust fund to reimburse actual 911 implementation, operation, call answering, and dispatching expenditures as deemed appropriate by the imposing local governing body.

headings.title: Exemption from general revenue transfer and interest retention
headings.reviewNote: Exempts unexpended trust fund balances from section 33.080 general revenue transfers and directs that earned interest remain in the fund.

headings.title: Non-state fund status and public local collection records
headings.reviewNote: Declares trust fund moneys not to be state funds and prohibits commingling, requiring the director of revenue to keep public, accurate collection records for each participating county, city not within a county, or qualifying home rule city.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the non-state Missouri 911 Service Trust Fund for fees remitted under sections 190.400 to 190.460, restricts use to 911 reimbursement and dispatch, exempts balances from general revenue transfer, and requires local collection records.

headings.title: Monthly 911 subscriber fee authorization
headings.reviewNote: Specifies conditions under which a county or city may impose a monthly 911 communications fee.

headings.title: Voter approval requirement and ballot language
headings.reviewNote: Requires voter approval for the monthly 911 fee and establishes standard ballot language.

headings.title: Mandatory ballot submission for charter counties
headings.reviewNote: Requires charter counties within a specified population bracket to submit the fee proposal by 2020.

headings.title: Application of general sales tax laws
headings.reviewNote: Applies statutory tax administration, enforcement, and refund provisions to the 911 fee.

headings.title: Collection, remittance, and administration of fees
headings.reviewNote: Governs remittance of collected fees to the trust fund and distribution to local governing bodies or boards.

headings.title: Provider enforcement and sourcing compliance
headings.reviewNote: Relieves communications providers from legal enforcement obligations and requires compliance with federal sourcing laws.

headings.title: Confidentiality of proprietary provider information
headings.reviewNote: Protects proprietary provider data from public disclosure except under subpoena or in aggregate form.

headings.title: Provider immunity from civil and criminal liability
headings.reviewNote: Grants immunity to communications service providers and personnel for emergency dispatch services and call location disclosures.

headings.title: Exemption for prospective or prepaid service
headings.reviewNote: Exempts prospective-pay customers and prepaid wireless telecommunications service from the subscriber fee.

headings.title: Prohibition on duplicative emergency taxes or fees
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits simultaneous imposition of the subscriber fee with other local emergency communications taxes.

headings.title: Consolidation or shared-services prerequisite for ballot
headings.reviewNote: Requires local emergency service consolidation or shared-services agreements prior to submitting ballot proposals.

headings.title: Consolidation plan filing and compliance deadlines
headings.reviewNote: Governs filing of consolidation plans with the state board and conditions for fee revocation upon noncompliance.

headings.title: Shared-services agreements or multi-county districts
headings.reviewNote: Directs counties without public emergency telephone providers to enter shared-services agreements or form joint districts.

headings.title: Voter proposal for consolidated operations
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes counties with joint emergency telephone services to submit fee proposals to support consolidation.

headings.title: Compliance with federal sourcing standards
headings.reviewNote: Requires all 911 fees to be imposed consistent with the federal Mobile Telecommunications Sourcing Act.

headings.title: Exception for existing charter county communications
headings.reviewNote: Exempts certain charter counties utilizing common 911 communication systems from specified consolidation mandates.

headings.title: Allocation agreements between multi-county cities and counties
headings.reviewNote: Mandates agreements between multi-county cities and counties regarding division of emergency revenue and regional service costs.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs county and municipal authority to impose monthly 911 communications subscriber fees upon voter approval, detailing collection, liability immunity, and dispatch consolidation requirements.

headings.title: Definitions for prepaid wireless service charges
headings.reviewNote: Defines board, consumer, prepaid wireless service provider, retail transaction, and related statutory terms.

headings.title: Imposition and collection of prepaid wireless charge
headings.reviewNote: Imposes a three percent prepaid wireless emergency telephone service charge beginning January 1, 2019 on retail transactions with the first fifteen dollars exempt, and sets nonitemized bundle, sourcing, consumer liability, and tax-base rules.

headings.title: Remittance, administration, and distribution of funds
headings.reviewNote: Regulates the remittance of prepaid service charges to the department and proportional distribution from the trust fund to counties and cities.

headings.title: Immunity and liability protections for sellers and providers
headings.reviewNote: Extends statutory civil and criminal liability protections to prepaid wireless sellers and providers.

headings.title: Service charge cumulative to other funding
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that the prepaid wireless emergency charge is in addition to other taxes or funding mechanisms.

headings.title: Local government opt-out procedure by two-thirds vote
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a mechanism for local governing bodies to prohibit collection of the prepaid charge by a two-thirds vote.

headings.title: Reversal of opt-out by governing body vote
headings.reviewNote: Permits governing bodies that opted out under subsection 6 to impose the charge by a two-thirds vote and department notice, requiring DOR to notify the board within sixty days; source note records an extra 'by' in original rolls.

entries.reviewSummary: Imposes a statewide prepaid wireless emergency telephone service charge, detailing collection procedures, trust fund distributions, liability protections, and local opt-out provisions.

headings.title: Definitions for declaratory ruling preemption provisions
headings.reviewNote: Defines all retail sales subject to sales tax, general retailer, and taxpayer; source note records original rolls read 'sections'.

headings.title: Declaratory ruling effect on retail sales tax preemption
headings.reviewNote: Provides seller relief and sets refund procedures if emergency sales taxes are declared preempted on all retail sales.

headings.title: Declaratory ruling effect on prepaid wireless service preemption
headings.reviewNote: Relieves sellers from retroactive tax assessments if emergency sales taxes are declared preempted on prepaid wireless services.

headings.title: Expiration date of preemption provisions
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the expiration date of January 1, 2023, for the statutory section.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes retailer protections, refund procedures, and liability limitations in the event of judicial declaratory rulings preempting local emergency telephone taxes.

headings.title: State policy encouraging emergency communications consolidation
headings.reviewNote: Declares state public policy promoting consolidation of emergency communications operations for efficiency and economy.

headings.title: Intergovernmental cooperation and advisory assistance
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes political subdivisions and emergency boards to contract jointly and seek advice from the Missouri 911 service board.

headings.title: Joint emergency communications entity establishment and governing body
headings.reviewNote: Permits establishing a joint emergency communications entity with equal governing board representation and requires a public written explanation to the Missouri 911 service board if the center is located outside the lowest-average-wage county.

headings.title: Approval required for answering point separation
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits separating existing public safety answering point operations without study and approval by the state board.

headings.title: Multiagency answering point operations permitted
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that consolidation rules do not prohibit or discourage forming multiagency or multijurisdictional answering points.

entries.reviewSummary: Articulates state policy encouraging consolidation of emergency communications operations, establishing contracting procedures, joint governing board guidelines, and oversight of answering point separations.

headings.title: Alternate consolidation procedure for dispatch centers
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes publicly funded 911 central dispatch centers to consolidate using an alternative petition or resolution process.

headings.title: Voter petition requirements for consolidation
headings.reviewNote: Specifies voter petition thresholds and filing procedures to request dispatch center consolidation.

headings.title: Form of consolidation petition
headings.reviewNote: Sets forth the required statutory petition text for consolidating existing 911 central dispatch centers.

headings.title: Board resolution procedure for consolidation
headings.reviewNote: Provides an alternative consolidation path through board of directors resolutions and prescribes resolution wording.

headings.title: Election order by county commission
headings.reviewNote: Directs county commissions to submit consolidation proposals to voters following receipt of valid petitions or resolutions.

headings.title: Notice of consolidation election
headings.reviewNote: Requires election notices to list the names of all existing central dispatch centers proposed for consolidation.

headings.title: Form of ballot question for consolidation
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes the mandatory ballot question wording submitted to voters for dispatch center consolidation.

headings.title: Consolidation order upon voter approval
headings.reviewNote: Directs county commissions to enter orders declaring consolidation passed upon majority approval in each service area.

headings.title: Appointment and composition of initial consolidated board
headings.reviewNote: Requires joint commission meetings to appoint a seven-member representative board for the consolidated center.

headings.title: Organizational meeting and naming of consolidated center
headings.reviewNote: Mandates an initial organizational meeting of the appointed board to select an official center name.

headings.title: Staggered terms and election of board members
headings.reviewNote: Establishes election timing, staggered term lengths, and at-large chairperson selection for the consolidated board.

headings.title: Transfer of powers, assets, and liabilities
headings.reviewNote: Dissolves predecessor dispatch centers thirty days after board appointment and transfers assets and liabilities to the consolidated center.

headings.title: Single-county existing board continuation vote
headings.reviewNote: Permits existing single-county emergency boards to vote whether to continue operations in lieu of dissolution.

entries.reviewSummary: Outlines an alternative voter-initiated or board-resolved procedure to consolidate public 911 central dispatch centers, governing elections, board appointments, and asset transfers.

headings.title: Temporary licensing of out-of-state health professionals
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes temporary licensure for out-of-state health professionals under military orders or emergency declarations.

headings.title: Verification and transmission of licensure information
headings.reviewNote: Permits licensure confirmation through electronic mail or other available transmission methods.

headings.title: Definition of health care professional
headings.reviewNote: Applies statutory definition of health care professional from section 383.130.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes issuance and renewal of temporary licenses for out-of-state health care professionals serving under military orders or declared emergencies.

headings.title: Stretcher van service licensure requirement
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits operating or advertising stretcher van services without first obtaining a department license.

headings.title: Municipal and county regulation limitations
headings.reviewNote: Restricts local political subdivisions from adopting unreasonable regulations to prevent stretcher van operations.

headings.title: Charter county standards and licensing authority
headings.reviewNote: Requires stretcher van services in high-population charter counties to obtain state licenses and comply with reasonable county standards.

headings.title: Preservation of existing political subdivision ambulance ordinances
headings.reviewNote: Preserves local ambulance laws and ordinances enacted prior to August 28, 2001.

headings.title: Authorized passenger transportation by stretcher vans
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes licensed stretcher van services to transport qualifying passengers.

headings.title: Staffing and automated external defibrillator requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires two-person staffing, an AED, and at least one AED-trained crew member on stretcher vans, and requires ambulance-authorized political subdivisions to adopt equally strict or stricter AED ordinances.

headings.title: Mandatory emergency ambulance notification upon passenger deterioration
headings.reviewNote: Requires stretcher van crews to contact ground ambulance services immediately if a passenger condition worsens.

headings.title: Prohibition on transporting emergency or admitted patients
